klook-data-bank-gift.content: Klook's official Data Bank campaign (2026-11-16 to 2026-12-31, or while gift boxes last): signed-in Klook users in qualifying markets can claim one mystery data gift box worth 0.5GB–50GB, with the larger amounts less likely; it's stored in the Data Bank as a "Gift from Klook", valid 180 days and resetting 180 days on each deposit. Claiming your own box unlocks 2–5 boxes to give to friends (0.5/1/3GB unlock 5 of the same size, 7GB unlocks 2×3.5GB, 15GB unlocks 3×5GB, 25GB unlocks 5×5GB, 50GB unlocks 5×10GB).
klook-data-bank-gift.conditions: Klook accounts resident in Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia or Vietnam only; one claim per account; Data Bank data must be added to a purchased eligible eSIM and can't be used as a standalone free eSIM; can't be combined with promo codes or vouchers on the same order; domestic-market eSIMs don't qualify; Argentina, Brunei, Central and South America, Colombia, Guam, Kenya, the Maldives, Mongolia, Nigeria, Panama, Greenland, Africa and Indian Ocean destinations aren't supported.
steps: Sign in with a qualifying Klook account and open the Data Bank campaign page on klook.com
Tap a gift box to claim the mystery data, revealed on the spot and stored in the Data Bank
When you next buy an eligible eSIM, add the Data Bank balance at checkout (gift data is used first)
To give to friends, use "Gift a friend" on the campaign page; they must also be in a qualifying market and can receive only one
klook-data-bank-gift.risk: The box is random and mostly small (0.5–3GB); you must buy an eSIM to use it, so it isn't free data on its own; residency is decided by the Klook profile and mainland Chinese accounts don't see the entry; the data isn't cash, can't be withdrawn and disappears if unused for 180 days.
klook-data-bank-gift.source: Klook official Data Bank campaign page + official T&C (databank_gtm_2026, markets limited to TW/TH/MY/VN, 2026-11-16 to 12-31)

taptap-send-referral.title: [Multi-region] Taptap Send: $10 off for new customers + $20 back for referrers
taptap-send-referral.highlight: Enter a referral code before your first transfer and both sides get credit; the recipient can't be the inviter
taptap-send-referral.regions: [Multi-region] Sending countries such as the US, UK, Germany, France, Spain, Italy and the Netherlands, each with its own minimum
taptap-send-referral.content: New users who register with Taptap Send, enter a referral code before their first transfer and complete a successful transfer at or above the app's minimum to a recipient who isn't the inviter get about $10 of credit; the inviter gets about $20 per success, up to 20 within 30 days.
taptap-send-referral.conditions: First-time users only; one code only; the first transfer must meet the minimum the app shows; cancelled transfers don't count.
steps: Download the app, register a new account and complete verification
Start the first transfer and enter the code under "Have a referral code?"
Confirm the recipient isn't the inviter and complete the transfer
Check the balance and use the reward within 90 days
taptap-send-referral.risk: The reward expires after 90 days and can't be withdrawn; amounts and minimums differ by sending and receiving country, so confirm the real numbers in the app.
taptap-send-referral.source: Taptap Send official referral terms + per-region code pages checked (2026-10)

nomad-trial-esim.title: [Global] Nomad free trial eSIM: 1GB / 3 days
nomad-trial-esim.highlight: Available in 76 countries and regions, no card needed, one-tap install in the app
nomad-trial-esim.regions: [Global] 76 popular destinations (including the US, much of Europe, Japan, Thailand, Turkey, Mexico and the UK); install within 15 days of departure
nomad-trial-esim.content: New Nomad users can claim a free 1GB / 3-day trial eSIM in the app, covering 76 destinations, with hotspot supported and no credit card. It can be installed up to 15 days ahead and activates automatically after 15 days if unused.
nomad-trial-esim.conditions: First-time Nomad users only; one per device and account; once claimed you lose other first-purchase offers or referral discounts.
steps: Download the Nomad app (iOS / Android) and register a new account with email
Choose your destination and claim the trial eSIM
Install it on Wi-Fi with one tap before you travel
It activates on arrival; use the 1GB within 3 days
nomad-trial-esim.risk: Claiming the trial means giving up the first-purchase discount, so compare prices first if you meant to buy a big plan; 1GB only covers navigation and messaging.
nomad-trial-esim.source: Nomad official trial page + help centre (2026-08-24)

saily-referral.title: [Global] Saily eSIM referral: $5 off, $10 on Ultra
saily-referral.highlight: $5 off your first order ($10 on Ultra), and the referrer gets the same in credits
saily-referral.content: Buy for the first time with a Saily user's referral code and get $5 off a standard plan or $10 off an Ultra plan (€4/€8 in the euro area); the referrer gets the same in Saily credits, valid for a year and usable against 100% of an order.
saily-referral.conditions: New users on their first purchase only; the order must exceed a minimum (about $5.60); can't be combined with promo codes; you can't use your own code.
steps: Download the Saily app and choose a destination and plan
After registering, go to Credits and enter your friend's referral code
Confirm the $5 is deducted at checkout
Install the eSIM and enable it at your destination
saily-referral.risk: Credits can't be withdrawn or transferred, and refunds cancel the referrer's credits; Saily has no free trial, so try Nomad or GigSky first if you want to test the network.
saily-referral.source: Saily official referral terms (updated 2026-09-25) + help centre

ubigi-welcome.title: [Multi-region] Ubigi 10% off your first order, 20% with an invite
ubigi-welcome.highlight: WELCOME10 takes 10% off your first order; through an invite link the first order can reach 20% off
ubigi-welcome.regions: [Multi-region] Japan, the US, Europe and 200+ countries and regions (the Japan local plans have the best reputation)
ubigi-welcome.content: Ubigi's official help centre lists WELCOME10 for 10% off the first data plan, in the app only and excluding monthly subscriptions. Registering through an existing user's invite link gives 20% off the first order, and the inviter gets a 50% off voucher in some regions.
ubigi-welcome.conditions: First purchase only; monthly plans are excluded; can't be combined with UbiCoins; invite terms differ by region.
steps: Choose a destination plan under Top up in the app
Enter WELCOME10 in the promo field for 10% off, or use the invite link for 20%
Check the discounted price, pay and install
ubigi-welcome.risk: The specific 20% invite rate is to be confirmed — the official page only guarantees the 10% from WELCOME10; monthly subscriptions take no discount at all.
ubigi-welcome.source: Ubigi official help centre + third-party price checks 2026-11 (the 20% invite rate is to be confirmed)

redbull-mobile-free-esim.title: [Global] Red Bull MOBILE free 1.1GB global eSIM (valid about 1 year / Austrian number range)
redbull-mobile-free-esim.highlight: Register for 100MB of global data free, then enter code TRAVELDEALZ in the app settings for another 1GB free — 1.1GB in total, valid about a year, with no credit card and no KYC
redbull-mobile-free-esim.regions: [Global] Global roaming data (an Austrian operator, so data roaming must be on abroad); tested and working from mainland China
redbull-mobile-free-esim.content: Red Bull MOBILE's data eSIM gives 100MB of global data free on registration; entering TRAVELDEALZ in the app's promo-code field orders another 1GB of global data free, 1.1GB in total, which the community finds stays valid for about a year. Registration needs only an email and a password — no credit card, no KYC — and it comes with an Austrian number range (data only, no texts). Once the data is used up you buy plans yourself.
redbull-mobile-free-esim.conditions: An eSIM-capable phone; email registration only; the TRAVELDEALZ code is added in the app settings; data only, no calls or texts; expires after about 6 months of no use; one per account/device.
steps: Download the Red Bull MOBILE app from the App Store or Google Play
Register with email and verify it
Tap "+" on the home screen to activate the eSIM (installing can wait) for the 100MB
Add TRAVELDEALZ in the app settings, then order the free 1GB global plan on the home screen
Abroad, turn on data and data roaming for that eSIM
redbull-mobile-free-esim.risk: To be confirmed: TRAVELDEALZ is a community-circulated campaign code that isn't published on the official site, so whether it still works depends on what the app shows at order time; a data-only SIM can't receive verification codes; it lapses if unused for a long time.
redbull-mobile-free-esim.source: A US card forum hands-on thread of 2026-09 (with install steps and data points from several countries); the promo-code field in the official app

moneygram-uk-invite-friends.title: [UK] MoneyGram invite friends: a discount on a new customer's first transfer (about £10, to be confirmed)
moneygram-uk-invite-friends.highlight: Existing customers send a personal link or code from Refer and Earn in the app or site, and a new customer uses it on their first online international transfer; the official wording only says the discount and minimum are whatever the Refer and Earn page shows, while third parties put it at £10
moneygram-uk-invite-friends.regions: [UK] UK (the transfer must go through moneygram.com or the MoneyGram app)
moneygram-uk-invite-friends.content: MoneyGram UK Invite Friends: an existing customer who has completed an online transfer can generate a personal link or code, a new customer registers with it and gets a discount on their first online international transfer, and the existing customer gets a discount once the friend's transfer arrives, up to 10 friends. The official Program Information (UK 2026) sets out only the mechanism and leaves the discount amount, minimum transfer and number of usable vouchers to the Refer and Earn page in the app, so no fixed figure is published — third-party deal sites (My Side Gig 2026-11-14 and coupon sites) all say £10. The new customer's discount doesn't expire, the existing customer's lasts 60 days, and neither can be combined with other promo codes; Plus Rewards members also get 50% off the second transfer's fee.
moneygram-uk-invite-friends.conditions: A new customer is anyone who has never opened an online MoneyGram profile (people who only sent in a store still count as new); the transfer must be online or in the app, not in a store; the amount and minimum are whatever the Refer and Earn page shows; one voucher per transfer and no stacking with other promotions.
steps: Ask a friend who has used MoneyGram for their Refer and Earn link or code
Register an online MoneyGram profile with that link and complete verification
Confirm the discount is applied on your first online international transfer (card payments don't get the related fee waiver)
Once it arrives, the existing customer's discount appears on their next transfer
moneygram-uk-invite-friends.risk: The amount isn't published — £10 comes from third parties, so confirm it in the app after registering; the discount covers only one transfer and can't be stacked; MoneyGram can change or end the programme at any time, and the FX spread is still there.
moneygram-uk-invite-friends.source: MoneyGram UK official Invite Friends page + Invite Friends Program Information (UK 2026) + My Side Gig's UK transfer ranking (2026-11-14, listing £10)

opera-android-free-esim-3gb.title: [Global] Opera for Android built-in eSIM: 3GB / 3 days free (47 destinations)
opera-android-free-esim-3gb.highlight: No card and no email: a few taps in Opera for Android gets 3GB, usable in Egypt, Turkey, South-East Asia and 47 places in all
opera-android-free-esim-3gb.regions: [Global] The free allowance is issued only in 11 markets: the US, UK, Germany, France, Canada, the UAE, Brazil, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and Poland; 47 destinations are covered (including Egypt, Turkey, Malaysia, Singapore, Japan, Korea and much of Europe, but not Gulf states such as the UAE and Saudi Arabia)
opera-android-free-esim-3gb.content: Opera has built travel eSIMs into Opera for Android (provided by Holiday.com): users in those 11 markets open the browser, tap Profile → eSIM → Claim now, choose a destination and get 3GB of free data valid 3 days, with no payment details and no email; the eSIM can be installed at home and only starts counting when it first connects to a destination network. Afterwards you can top up 3GB / 5GB / 10GB (valid 30 days) on the same eSIM by country, which Opera says is about 33% cheaper on average than mainstream eSIM providers.
opera-android-free-esim-3gb.conditions: Must be Opera for Android installed from Google Play (not Opera Mini or mobile Opera GX), Android 10 or later, with an eSIM-capable unlocked phone; the free 3GB only goes to users located in those 11 countries; one eSIM per phone; the destination must be on the list of 47.
steps: Install or update Opera for Android from Google Play
Tap the profile icon at the bottom right, scroll to eSIM and tap Claim now
Choose and confirm the destination country
Install the eSIM on Wi-Fi
Turn on data roaming on arrival and the 3 days start
opera-android-free-esim-3gb.risk: Users in mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and elsewhere aren't in the free list and can only buy paid plans; the 47 destinations exclude Gulf states such as the UAE and Saudi Arabia, so it's no use for the Middle East; the wrong install source or version hides the claim entry.
opera-android-free-esim-3gb.source: Opera official press release (2026-09-29) + Opera Mobile blog claim steps + esim.operacdn.com help page (rechecked 2026-11-19)

remitly-uk-cashback.title: [UK] Remitly new-customer cashback: TopCashback £8 / Quidco £6.40 (stackable with the first-transfer offer)
remitly-uk-cashback.highlight: New customers click through from a cashback site, register via the link and send a first transfer of £100+: TopCashback £8, Quidco £6.40 (Premium rate), KidStart up to £15; Remitly's own first-transfer fee waiver or rate boost applies at the same time, but don't add third-party promo codes
remitly-uk-cashback.regions: [UK] UK senders only; this is not the same as the US $20–$25 coupons
remitly-uk-cashback.content: The cashback route for new UK Remitly customers (checked 2026-11-19): click "Get cashback" on a UK cashback site's Remitly page, register a UK Remitly account in the same browser session and complete a first international transfer, and the site pays a fixed amount. TopCashback UK currently pays £8 (new customers, first transfer of £100+); Quidco shows £6.40 but marks it as the Premium rate, with standard members getting about £6; KidStart pays up to £15 by tier, though the money goes into a linked child's savings account and can't be withdrawn directly; ShopBuddies up to £8 and Rakuten up to £7. Cashback usually shows as pending within 24 hours and becomes withdrawable only once Remitly confirms the transfer qualifies (Quidco states payment within 6 months). In the same signup, Remitly's own first-transfer offers (fee waiver, rate boost, first-transfer discount — whatever the registration page finally quotes) usually apply automatically and stack with the cashback; but cashback sites generally void it for "using promo codes not approved by us", so entering a third-party referral code or coupon risks losing the cashback.
remitly-uk-cashback.conditions: New Remitly customers only (never registered or sent); first transfer of at least £100 (both TopCashback and Quidco terms say £100, though some comparison sites still show £200 — the order page decides); you must arrive through the cashback site's link and finish registration and payment in the same browser session with ad blockers and coupon extensions off; TopCashback excludes unapproved promo codes and Quidco excludes extra discount codes that reduce the transaction value, so stacking a friend's referral code can void it; Quidco's £6.40 needs Premium (£1 a month taken from cashback, often free to try for new members).
steps: Register or sign in to TopCashback UK or Quidco (or check GotCashback first to see who pays most that day)
Search Remitly on the cashback site and click Get cashback, with ad blockers and coupon extensions off
Register a new UK Remitly account in the same browser session, complete KYC and confirm the first-transfer offer has applied
Send a first transfer of £100+ to a third-party recipient (not yourself and not the inviter) and let it be delivered
Check the pending record on the cashback site within 24 hours; it becomes withdrawable after the merchant confirms (Quidco up to 6 months)
remitly-uk-cashback.risk: The "$25 off Remitly" links circulating online are almost all US-only codes and do nothing in the UK; cashback is confirmed after the fact, so a cancelled transfer, closed account or merchant rejection means nothing at all — don't budget it into the first transfer; KidStart's £15 is a tier cap and only goes into a child's savings account; "fee-free" usually just moves the cost into the FX spread, so compare what the recipient actually receives.
remitly-uk-cashback.source: TopCashback UK Remitly merchant page (rechecked 2026-11-19: new customers £8, first transfer £100+; the official site returns 403 to non-UK IPs, so terms were cross-checked against search caches and comparison sites) + Quidco Remitly merchant page (captured 2026-11-19: £6.40 is the Premium rate, first transfer from £100, tracked within 24 hours, paid within 6 months) + GotCashback comparison page (captured 2026-11-18: KidStart up to £15, ShopBuddies up to £8, Rakuten up to £7, all tier caps) + Remitly UK referral page and referral terms (friend's first-transfer discount / rate boost / fee waiver, amounts vary by campaign)

hoody-free-cloud-computers.title: [Global] Hoody 3 free Linux cloud computers: no card, no expiry (root included)
hoody-free-cloud-computers.highlight: Sign up for 3 Linux cloud computers sharing 2 cores / 3GB RAM / 20GB storage and 10Mbps, with full root and systemd, no card and no trial limit, plus 5 .hoody.bot bot domains
hoody-free-cloud-computers.regions: [Global] Hoody shared hosting (you can request a preferred region, subject to capacity and fallback); the free tier excludes KVM virtual machines
hoody-free-cloud-computers.content: Hoody sells Linux hosts where each cloud computer is reachable at its own URL; the free tier is $0/mo, needs no card and doesn't expire: up to 3 computers sharing 2 CPU cores, 3GB of RAM, 20GB of storage and 10Mbps, with 2 snapshots each, plus 5 .hoody.bot bot domains, 5 Realms and a free Hoody AI allowance. With root and systemd you can run code, a browser, a GUI desktop, scheduled jobs and HTTP services (bind a port and the URL is published), and mount cloud storage (S3, Google Drive, Dropbox, WebDAV) for backups. Good for practice, small scripts, a temporary site or browser automation. The paid Plus tier at $10/mo gives 12 computers (3 cores/6GB/75GB, 8 regions).
hoody-free-cloud-computers.conditions: The free allowance is shared across all three computers; hosts are shared with others and capacity is limited, so the region chosen at signup is only a preference; no virtual machines (that needs the paid Bare Metal tier); the models and availability of the Hoody AI allowance aren't guaranteed; activity and capacity limits can change at any time.
steps: Open hoody.com and sign up (no credit card needed)
Claim the free server and open the web terminal or log in over SSH
Install dependencies and run scripts; for a public service, bind the port and the URL is published
Sync important files to external storage so they aren't lost when the instance is cleaned up
hoody-free-cloud-computers.risk: The free tier has no SLA on shared hosts, so resources can be reclaimed or changed at any time; don't keep the only copy of important data there; the platform is new and its terms and free policy can change.
hoody-free-cloud-computers.source: Hoody official pricing page (checked 2026-11-19 for the free-tier specs and "no card / 3 computers")

touch-lebanon-magic-welcome-3gb.title: [LB] touch new-card welcome: 3GB a month × 3 months (buy a $7 Magic prepaid card)
touch-lebanon-magic-welcome-3gb.highlight: Pay $7 for a new Magic prepaid card and get 3GB a month for three months; the offer runs to 12/14
touch-lebanon-magic-welcome-3gb.regions: [LB] Lebanon only; needs a Lebanese number (the online eSIM signup currently requires a Lebanese passport)
touch-lebanon-magic-welcome-3gb.content: touch's Magic prepaid welcome: buy a new Magic prepaid card for $7 (before tax) and get 3GB of free data each month for three consecutive months, 9GB in total, with the offer valid to 2026-12-14. It goes with touch's fully digital eSIM signup launched on 2026-10-23: pick a number in the touch app, scan a Lebanese passport, pass a face check and sign electronically to activate a prepaid eSIM within minutes, without visiting a store.
touch-lebanon-magic-welcome-3gb.conditions: Must buy a new Magic prepaid card ($7 before tax); the free data is issued monthly and the card must be opened during the campaign; the online eSIM signup is limited to Lebanese passport holders (national ID support comes later); documents required for in-store activation follow store rules (to be confirmed).
steps: Update the touch app and open Digital Onboarding
Pick a number, scan your Lebanese passport, complete the face check and sign electronically
Choose eSIM and pay the $7 card fee online
After activation 3GB arrives each month for 3 months
touch-lebanon-magic-welcome-3gb.risk: You pay $7 up front for the card and the online signup needs a Lebanese passport, so non-Lebanese users are effectively shut out; the free data is local only, issued monthly and not replaced if it expires; the offer ends 14 December.
touch-lebanon-magic-welcome-3gb.source: touch official campaign page (offer valid until December 14th 2026) + touch's digital onboarding launch (2026-10-23) and LeBusiness coverage

teleagent-free-cloud-pc.title: [CN] China Telecom TeleAgent Xingshen: a Windows cloud PC in the free tier
teleagent-free-cloud-pc.highlight: Log in on the web and use the built-in Windows cloud PC (the community measured 4 cores); the free trial tier is ¥0/mo with 3 parallel tasks, long-term memory, a secure sandbox, scheduled tasks and a skills marketplace
teleagent-free-cloud-pc.regions: [CN] China Telecom's TeleAgent web and desktop apps; needs a Chinese mobile number to register
teleagent-free-cloud-pc.content: China Telecom's in-house TeleAgent (Xingshen super agent) offers a free trial tier at ¥0/mo with 3 concurrent tasks, long-term memory, a secure sandbox, scheduled tasks, multimodal abilities and an official skills marketplace, plus free credits from the Credits Welfare Store. The official site says the web app includes a Windows cloud PC that works as soon as you open the page, and the community measured 4 cores, which suits running Windows software temporarily or as a light cloud desktop. The paid personal plan starts at ¥34/mo (currently 30% off).
teleagent-free-cloud-pc.conditions: An account is required (Chinese mobile number); the free tier has a monthly credit allowance, topped up from the welfare store or by buying boost packs; the cloud PC's specs and per-session time limit aren't published on the pricing page, so the login page decides; at most 3 concurrent tasks.
steps: Open ta.teleai.com.cn, register and sign in
On the web app, click the top-right entry for the cloud PC
Install Windows software or run tasks on the cloud PC as needed
When credits run low, claim free credits from the Credits Welfare Store
teleagent-free-cloud-pc.risk: To be confirmed: the cloud PC specs (the community says 4 cores) and the free allowance's duration aren't stated on the official pricing page; free credits are limited; a domestic product needs a real-name mobile number, so mind data compliance.
teleagent-free-cloud-pc.source: TeleAgent official pricing page and home page (free trial tier at ¥0/mo, built-in Windows cloud PC) + NodeLoc hands-on thread of 2026-11-18

cloady-free-tier.title: [Global] Cloady free container cloud: 0.5 vCPU / 1GB RAM / 5GB SSD, no card
cloady-free-tier.highlight: Sign in with an email code and open a free workspace for blogs, bots, small APIs or uptime probes, with TLS and an xxx.cloady.io subdomain, and no card at any point
cloady-free-tier.regions: [Global] Free-tier regions are EU1 Germany, USE1 US East and USW1 US West (Japan isn't taking new free apps; Singapore, the UK and India aren't open)
cloady-free-tier.content: Cloady is NeptoLab's PaaS (similar to Railway / Render) billed by declared CPU, memory and SSD, with a free tier and free trials in some regions: a whole workspace within 0.5 vCPU, 1GB of RAM and 5GB of SSD is $0/mo, and only beyond that does it need a card. It supports deploy-on-push from GitHub, Docker images, direct directory uploads and a template marketplace (WordPress, Vaultwarden, Nginx Proxy Manager and more); each web app gets an xxx.cloady.io subdomain and TLS automatically, and there's a REST API, CLI, Terraform and MCP. The new terms apply to new accounts from 2026-11-02.
cloady-free-tier.conditions: Register with a real mailbox that receives mail (temporary mailboxes and bulk signups are banned); the free quota is shared across the workspace, so several apps will exceed it; going over without a card prompts an upgrade rather than charging automatically; mining, Tor, IRC and similar uses are banned; free-tier and trial regions can change at any time.
steps: Open cloady.com, register with your usual email and complete the code login
The workspace is created automatically; click Deploy and choose a GitHub repo, image, directory upload or template
Pick EU1, USE1 or USW1, keep resources within the workspace's free quota and confirm the page shows $0.00/mo
Open the assigned cloady.io domain after deployment (if a Docker image's port isn't detected, use a Dockerfile with EXPOSE or specify the port in the API)
cloady-free-tier.risk: "Free forever" is a community claim — the official site only promises a free tier plus free trials in some regions, and users report it becoming free for one month, so long-term availability is unclear; the free specs are tiny, so a real site will exceed them; the Japan region has workspaces but restricted free apps, so choose the region manually.
cloady-free-tier.source: Cloady official pricing and free-tier page (rechecked 2026-11-19) + a 1A2X community hands-on thread of 2026-11-13 (with limits and pitfalls)

woori-bank-esim-1gb.title: [KR] Woori Bank: exchange currency and get a free 1GB overseas eSIM (11/17–12/31, first 20,000)
woori-bank-esim-1gb.highlight: Make an FX exchange in Hwanjeon Jumeoni in the app first (any amount, any currency) and the first 20,000 customers get a free 1GB overseas data eSIM covering 130+ countries, valid for a year after registration
woori-bank-esim-1gb.regions: [KR] Woori Bank (Woori WON Banking) customers in Korea; the eSIM works in 130+ countries abroad
woori-bank-esim-1gb.content: Woori Bank's official campaign (2026-11-17 to 2026-12-31, first 20,000, ending early once they run out): complete one exchange request in Hwanjeon Jumeoni in Woori WON Banking (mobile FX with cash pickup at a branch) for any amount and currency, then open the campaign page from the pop-up or banner on the completion screen and download the eSIM from Woori's page in the partner "THE LOUNGE" app. The prize is a download voucher for a 1GB overseas data eSIM covering more than 130 countries, valid for a year after registration, once per account during the campaign, on an eSIM-compatible handset.
woori-bank-esim-1gb.conditions: Must be a Woori Bank customer and complete an exchange in Hwanjeon Jumeoni in Woori WON Banking; first 20,000, while stocks last; THE LOUNGE app must be installed to claim; the phone must support eSIM; one per person; the data voucher can't be transferred.
steps: Sign in to Woori WON Banking and submit an exchange in Hwanjeon Jumeoni (any amount, any currency)
Tap the pop-up or banner on the completion screen to open the Woori campaign page
Install THE LOUNGE app, then claim and download the 1GB eSIM on Woori's page
Enable the eSIM when travelling (valid for a year after registration)
woori-bank-esim-1gb.risk: You need a Korean Woori Bank account and must actually exchange some currency (the money stays yours, but it's tied up); only 20,000 places, first come first served; the THE LOUNGE app is required; 1GB is only enough for emergencies, not your main data.
woori-bank-esim-1gb.source: Woori Bank official campaign announcement (from 2026-11-17) + same-day coverage by several Korean outlets including NewsPim and Hyundai Economy TV (details agree)

simular-box-free.title: [Global] box by Simular: a free cloud Linux desktop (5,000 credits ≈ 50 hours / 90 days)
simular-box-free.highlight: Sign up for 5,000 credits (1,000 credits = $1) and give an AI a real cloud Linux desktop: it can open a browser, click, read the screen and run commands
simular-box-free.regions: [Global] Sign up online; connects to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex and other MCP-capable clients as a remote MCP server
simular-box-free.content: box is Simular's cloud Linux desktop; connected to an AI client as a remote MCP server, the AI can really open a browser, click, type, read the screen and run commands. Each account gets one desktop, which sleeps when idle; the free tier gives 5,000 credits one-off (1,000 credits = $1, about 50 hours of box time, valid 90 days), and the paid tiers are S at $19/mo and M at $39/mo (M doesn't sleep). A box asleep for 14 consecutive days is deleted.
simular-box-free.conditions: Register a Simular account and authorise the MCP server via OAuth; the 5,000 free credits are one-off and valid 90 days; the AI itself still needs its own subscription or API; free boxes sleep when idle and are deleted after 14 days without waking.
steps: Register and sign in at box.simular.ai
Add https://mcp.box.simular.ai/mcp as a remote MCP server in your AI client
Authorise with your Simular account on the first connection
Let the AI run tasks on the cloud desktop (open a browser, run commands, edit files)
simular-box-free.risk: Beyond the free credits it's billed per credit, so don't let the AI spin idle; the desktop holds your browser session, so don't sign into important accounts inside it.
simular-box-free.source: box by Simular official page (free allowance and billing)

horizon-free-europe-esim.title: [Europe + UK] Horizon free 1GB eSIM (30 days / 33 countries)
horizon-free-europe-esim.highlight: New and existing users can claim once: 1GB shared across 33 European countries, valid 30 days, claimed in the app, no card
horizon-free-europe-esim.regions: [Europe + UK] 33 countries: most of the EU plus the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Ukraine; excluding Turkey, Serbia, Bosnia, Montenegro, Albania and North Macedonia (per the official list)
horizon-free-europe-esim.content: Horizon's entry promo: open the "Europe" destination in the Horizon app, choose the 1GB / 30-day plan, verify your email and WhatsApp number and claim it for €0. The entry offer is once per account and verified number — reinstalling the app or a refund doesn't restore eligibility.
horizon-free-europe-esim.conditions: App only (iOS 15+ / Android); an eSIM-capable, carrier-unlocked phone (mainland-China iPhones need their overseas-eSIM restriction checked); email and WhatsApp verification required; once per account and number; the free plan needs no payment card, but paid add-ons on the same order are charged; data only, no number.
steps: Download the Horizon app (App Store / Google Play) and sign in
Open the Europe destination and choose 1GB / 30 days (shown at €0.00, once only)
Verify your email and WhatsApp number and claim it
Install the eSIM on Wi-Fi in advance; on arrival set it as the mobile data line and turn on data roaming for it
horizon-free-europe-esim.risk: It only covers 33 European countries, so it's no use in Turkey or parts of the Balkans; you need a number that can receive a WhatsApp code; when the 1GB runs out it doesn't become a paid subscription, but there's no more data either.
horizon-free-europe-esim.source: Horizon official free Europe page + official Europe plan page (1GB/30 days at €0.00, PROMO once only); NodeSeek post-1055219, NodeLoc topic/117906, 1A2X t/881 and Naixi forum thread-16496 (2026-11-15)

kolet-virgin-atlantic-free-esim.title: [Global] Kolet × Virgin Atlantic: free 1GB eSIM (about 2 days)
kolet-virgin-atlantic-free-esim.highlight: Claim 1GB straight from the Virgin Atlantic partner page, about two days of use, no card needed, covering 190 countries; once per device
kolet-virgin-atlantic-free-esim.regions: [Global] 190 countries and regions; forum testing found it works from mainland China (roaming on China Mobile/Unicom, egress in Poland or the UK)
kolet-virgin-atlantic-free-esim.content: Kolet's landing page with Virgin Atlantic (virginatlantic.shop.kolet.com) gives 1GB of free data, which the official wording puts at about 2 days of mobile use, with no credit card and no contract, covering 190 destinations. steps: Open virginatlantic.shop.kolet.com and tap "Try Kolet for free" at the top
Download the Kolet app, register with email and verify the phone number
To use it in China, choose China as the destination and claim the free 1GB
Scan the QR code to install the eSIM and turn on data roaming; top up in the app when it runs out
kolet-virgin-atlantic-free-esim.risk: Only about 2 days, then it stops; one free claim per device and reinstalling doesn't help (the community calls it "black EID"); claiming needs phone verification, and virtual numbers may be blocked.
kolet-virgin-atlantic-free-esim.source: Kolet x Virgin Atlantic partner page (still offering the free 1GB in 2026-11) plus Virgin Atlantic's own Kolet page at virginatlantic.com/en-EU/experience/upgrades-and-extras/kolet (checked 2026-11-21: 1GB, about two days, no card) and the NodeSeek thread 1051360 (2026-11-13) with NodeLoc and Naixi forum tests the same day

nala-uk-first-transfer-5.title: [UK] NALA first-transfer reward: £5 (down from £10 recently)
nala-uk-first-transfer-5.highlight: New UK customers register with an invite code and send a first transfer of £50+; the reward lands in the Reward Wallet and covers the whole next transfer with no fee; the reward dropped from £10 to £5 in November
nala-uk-first-transfer-5.regions: [UK] UK registration (UK IP, UK phone number, UK card, passport KYC); common destinations are the Philippines' Maya wallet and African/Asian corridors
nala-uk-first-transfer-5.content: NALA's Invite a Friend: a new customer enters the invite code when registering, and after a qualifying first transfer the reward lands in the Reward Wallet, covering the whole of the next transfer (the official note says the minimum usable is 5 £/€/$). In the UK it was "send £50, get £10" in early November, but around 11-10 many users reported it had dropped to £5; the official help centre only says the amount is whatever the app's Earn page shows and lists the UK minimum transfer as £100 — which doesn't match the community's £50, so this is to be confirmed.
nala-uk-first-transfer-5.conditions: NALA new customers only; the invite code can only be entered at registration and can't be added after sending; first transfer of £50+ (the official help page says £100, to be confirmed); needs a UK IP, UK time zone, UK phone number, UK card and passport KYC, with the card's billing address matching the registered address; the reward only offsets transfers and can't be withdrawn.
steps: Set your phone's time zone to the UK, connect through a UK IP and download the NALA app
Enter the invite code at registration and complete KYC with passport, NFC and a face scan
Send a first transfer of £50+ to the Philippines' Maya (arrives in minutes, no fee)
See the £5 in the Reward Wallet and use it in full on the next transfer
nala-uk-first-transfer-5.risk: The reward fell from £10 to £5 and can close early "because of demand"; the official minimum is £100 while the community reports £50 — the two don't agree; mismatched address, time zone or IP can get the payment refused or the account banned; the reward only offsets a transfer and can't be cashed out.
nala-uk-first-transfer-5.source: NALA official help centre (Invite a Friend, minimum transfer) + several NodeSeek hands-on threads of 2026-11-12 (£10 now £5) + an aijp.jizhiku.net tutorial of 2026-11-11 (still saying £10)

steps: Open xl.co.id/esim-trial and tap Ambil Disini
Register with email and choose a number
Follow the email or SMS to complete real-name checks and install the eSIM
Use the 5GB within 7 days, then buy a plan in myXL to continue

Turn on data roaming on arrival and use the 2GB within 7 days

garuda-esim-free-2gb.source: Garuda eSIM by Yoowifi official site (read 2026-11-19: Free 2GB / 7 days, Claim Complimentary eSIM, 160+ countries) + coverage of Garuda Indonesia's launch on 2026-10-01 (Kompas, Bisnis, Marketing-Interactive)

jetpac-eterna-free-esim.title: [Global] Jetpac Eterna lifetime free eSIM: 4 × 100MB a year
jetpac-eterna-free-esim.highlight: Claim once and it lasts for life: 100MB per trip, up to 4 times a year (2 months apart); WhatsApp / Google Maps / Uber / Grab use zero data (throttled to 1Mbps)
jetpac-eterna-free-esim.regions: [Global] Works on international roaming (forum testing from mainland China roams on China Mobile/Unicom with a Singapore IP); only for eligible users in the US, UK, Australia, Canada, Germany, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, New Zealand and France — other countries join a waitlist
jetpac-eterna-free-esim.content: Jetpac Eterna is a "lifetime free" travel eSIM: once registered and claimed, the eSIM stays valid and arrives with 100MB, and every 2 months you can claim another 100MB in the app, up to 4 times a year (about 400MB in total). Even after the 100MB is gone, WhatsApp, Google Maps, Uber and Grab keep working without limit (throttled to about 1Mbps) and don't use the free allowance. It's data only, with no number and no calls or texts, and works only while roaming abroad, not at home. NodeSeek threads of 2026-10-07 and 11-04, the Naixi forum on 10-07 and the Shaobing forum on 11-04 all report "restocked again".
jetpac-eterna-free-esim.conditions: Only for eligible users in the US, UK, Australia, Canada, Germany, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, New Zealand and France, and registration needs a phone number from one of them for the code (forums report Google Voice passes); must be installed in the Jetpac app; can't be used as domestic data; one account per person; anyone with a paid Jetpac plan has to wait until it ends; contact support before changing phones or reinstalling.
steps: Open the Jetpac Eterna claim page, tap redeem and fill in name, mobile and email
Choose the US or Canada as the country (it goes through more smoothly) and verify with a number that receives codes
Download the Jetpac app, sign in with the same email and install the eSIM
Enable the line abroad; after that you can claim another 100MB in the app every 2 months
jetpac-eterna-free-esim.risk: 100MB a time is very little and only an arrival stopgap; the official terms limit it to eligible international roaming and exclude domestic use; the zero-data apps are only those four and throttled to 1Mbps, so it's not main data.
jetpac-eterna-free-esim.source: Jetpac official Eterna page (eligibility, 4 times a year and the zero-data apps are all stated); NodeSeek post-969696 / 969051 (2026-10-07), post-1030534 (2026-11-04), Naixi forum thread-15892 (2026-10-07), Shaobing forum t/16798 (2026-11-04)

eskimo-free-esim.title: [Global] Eskimo free 500MB global eSIM (126 countries / no expiry)
eskimo-free-esim.highlight: Enter FREE500MB as the referral or gift code when signing up for 500MB of free global data covering 126 countries and regions, with no expiry and no credit card
eskimo-free-esim.regions: [Global] 126+ countries and regions (including Japan, China, the US, Italy and Thailand); new users only
eskimo-free-esim.content: Travel eSIM brand Eskimo (Datapro, Singapore) free trial: new users installing the app enter FREE500MB under "referral or gift code" at signup and get 500MB of global data covering more than 126 countries and regions. The official page says no credit card, one install works in many countries, and the data doesn't expire, which suits maps, rides and messages on arrival. The earlier FREE250MB tier may still work on some accounts, and limited 1GB gift codes such as EDC1GB and OKZMO circulate in the community (their validity isn't confirmed on the official page and they're time-limited acquisition campaigns that can stop at any moment).
eskimo-free-esim.conditions: Eskimo new users only; the code must be entered at signup in the app (if missed, it can be added within 24 hours after registering); one per account; the data doesn't expire, but accounts unused for about 2 years are deleted; mainland-China phones without native eSIM support must ask support for a QR code and write it to a blank eUICC card (APN Singtel Postpaid; don't delete it after installing).
steps: Download the Eskimo app (developer Datapro Technologies)
Register a new account with email or Google and enter FREE500MB as the referral or gift code
Check the Data page for the Global 500MB plan
Install directly on an eSIM-capable phone, or ask support for the QR code to write to a blank card on a mainland-China handset
On arrival set mobile data to that eSIM and turn on data roaming
eskimo-free-esim.risk: 500MB is only enough for emergencies (a few hours of maps and messages) with no calls; the 1GB gift codes are time-limited and their amount and validity aren't confirmed officially; mainland-China phones need an extra blank eUICC card, and a failed write has to be redone.
eskimo-free-esim.source: Eskimo official free data promo page (eskimo.travel, FREE500MB tier) + several hands-on reports from 2026-11 (including in-app screenshots of the credit)

gohub-free-trial-esim.title: [12 Asian countries] GoHub free trial eSIM: 300MB / 1 day
gohub-free-trial-esim.highlight: New users get 300MB of high-speed data in the app, valid 1 day, across 12 Asian destinations including China, Japan, Korea, Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand, with no card needed
gohub-free-trial-esim.regions: [12 Asian countries] China, Japan, Korea, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines, Hong Kong, Taiwan and India (per the destination list on the claim page)
gohub-free-trial-esim.content: GoHub's one-off free trial eSIM for new users: 300MB of high-speed data valid 1 day, for 12 Asian destinations (mainland China included). steps: Download the GoHub app from the App Store or Google Play and register
Find "Free Trial eSIM" in the app and choose your Asian destination
Install the eSIM as prompted (you can install it at home on Wi-Fi without using the trial data)
On arrival set GoHub as the mobile data line and turn on data roaming — the clock starts on first connection
gohub-free-trial-esim.risk: Only 300MB / 1 day, enough for a ride, navigation and a few messages but not a whole day; it stops when the data runs out with no charge and no auto-renewal; don't treat a 1-day trial as main data for a whole trip.
gohub-free-trial-esim.source: GoHub official claim page + official blog (updated 2026-11-17); recommended in the same thread on NodeSeek post-1055219, NodeLoc topic/117906, 1A2X t/881 and Naixi forum thread-16496 (all 2026-11-15), with a test from mainland China roaming on China Unicom at about 40Mbps

gomoworld-free-trial-esim.title: [Multi-region] GoMoWorld free trial eSIM: up to 1GB / 1 day

gomoworld-free-trial-esim.conditions: Claimed in the app only, with the amount shown per destination; once per new user; an eSIM-capable unlocked phone; valid 1 day only, meant as an arrival-day stopgap; the app store description says "up to 1GB free, no bank card needed" but no separate trial terms are published, so what the app shows at claim time applies.
steps: Download the GoMoWorld app (iOS / Android) and register
Choose the destination and claim the free trial on its page (amounts vary by country)
Install the eSIM as prompted (at home on Wi-Fi first)
Enable the eSIM at the destination and turn on data roaming; the 1 day starts then
gomoworld-free-trial-esim.risk: The amount varies by destination and it lasts only 1 day; the roughly 100MB for mainland China comes from forum testing and isn't published officially, so test small first; don't expect it to cover a whole day.
gomoworld-free-trial-esim.source: GoMoWorld official app store description (updated 2026-11) + official FAQ + third-party per-provider check (2026-10-31); recommended in the same thread across four forums on 2026-11-15

roroesim-cs-trial-300mb.title: [Global] Roro eSIM: 300MB of test data from support (800 days)

Scroll to the bottom, click Contact us → live chat and ask for a test
Install the QR code you're given and check the plan shows 800 days after activation
It can sit unused as an emergency backup; turn on data roaming when you use it

roroesim-cs-trial-300mb.source: Naixi forum thread-16230 (2026-10-27, with hands-on screenshots and several user reports); the official site only states that physical cards come with 300MB of global data, while the eSIM test pack is issued by support with no published terms (to be confirmed)

ooredoo-qatar-easysim-welcome.title: [QA] Ooredoo EasySIM welcome: a free new card + 300MB / 3 days

iroamly-free-500mb-trial.title: [Global] iRoamly free trial eSIM: 500MB / 1 day (100+ destinations)

Install the eSIM and turn on data roaming on arrival

roamless-free-trial-500mb.highlight: Install one global eSIM for $1.25 of credit — about 500MB — with no card and no expiry
roamless-free-trial-500mb.regions: [Global] One global eSIM for 200+ countries and regions; a few destinations have the free allowance switched off (per the app)

roamless-free-trial-500mb.conditions: Roamless new users only, one per account/device; download the app, register and install the eSIM; the free credit lands automatically after activation; a few destinations don't offer it.

Tap Install eSIM on the home screen and install the Roamless eSIM
Set it as the mobile data line as prompted

pickle-ai-free-agent-jpkr.title: [JP/KR] Pickle: a free AI agent that calls and browses the web for you
pickle-ai-free-agent-jpkr.highlight: Books, orders and fills forms in its own cloud browser — and phones the place itself when a site can't (restaurants, clinics, landlords, support), with the call audible live. Japan/Korea accounts are free, the daily limit resets at 4 AM and reset tickets continue.
pickle-ai-free-agent-jpkr.regions: [JP/KR] Japan and Korea: every account is free with no paid plan, and the daily limit resets at 04:00 local time. The English (US) help pages still list Plus / Pro / Max / Ultra weekly subscriptions (paid). What the app shows under My Pickle → Daily usage limit is what applies.
pickle-ai-free-agent-jpkr.content:
Pickle is a personal AI agent that actually does the work rather than only chatting. Two things define it. First, a cloud browser: the official help says Pickle uses a real web browser to work sites the way a person would — booking restaurants and flights, buying things, cancelling subscriptions, reading bank and brokerage records, requesting documents on government sites. That browser lives in the cloud, separate from your phone, and if a step only you can do comes up (a CAPTCHA, or you'd rather type your own password) the screen is handed to you to finish. Second, phone calls: for places with no booking page — a restaurant, a clinic's front desk, your landlord, a customer service line — Pickle calls for you, the call can be followed live, the result is reported back, and the record sits in Other chats.

Before a payment or booking it shows a card of what it will do and at what price and waits for your go-ahead; if the amount rises right before paying, it asks again.

Free plan (per the Japanese help centre): in Japan every account is free with no paid plan, replaced by a daily usage limit that resets to 0% at 04:00 Japan time. Replies, calls from Chat, handed-off tasks and scheduled tasks all count; conversations on 3D World calls and Pickle's own fixed routines do not. At the limit the input box turns off and scheduled tasks are skipped until 04:00.

Reset tickets: a Full reset ticket returns the day's usage to 0%; a Half reset ticket lowers it by 50 points (never below 0%). You get one Full ticket for finishing onboarding, one each for you and each friend who completes sign-up through your invite link, and you can buy more in the app at prices shown on the purchase screen (the US App Store lists $3.99 for a Full ticket and $1.99 for a Half ticket; Japan about ¥600 each — it varies by store). Tickets don't expire and only restore the current day's usage; they don't raise the daily cap.
pickle-ai-free-agent-jpkr.conditions: Applies automatically to Japan/Korea accounts, with no card or subscription needed. A ticket only restores usage already spent that day and does not raise the daily cap; unused tickets stay but the day's usage resets anyway at 04:00. Once the limit is reached, new tasks can't start and scheduled tasks are skipped. The app runs on iOS and Android only (no web version).
steps: Install Pickle from the App Store or Google Play and finish sign-up (Japan/Korea accounts are free, no card)
Say what you need in Chat, e.g. "Book a table for two at 7 PM Friday and ask if they have parking"
Pickle works the site in its cloud browser; where a site can't help, it calls and the call shows in Other chats
Check the task card for what it will do and what it will cost, then let it run (it always checks before paying or booking)
Out of usage: My Pickle → Daily usage limit → use a reset ticket, or continue right away from the "Continue using" card
Want more tickets: invite friends — you and each friend who completes sign-up get one Full reset ticket
pickle-ai-free-agent-jpkr.risk: Terms differ sharply by region: the Japanese and Korean help pages say all accounts are free with no paid plan, while the English (US) pages still require a subscription and list Plus/Pro/Max/Ultra, so check the card in your own app. A ticket only rescues the current day and does not raise the base limit. Pickle has not published the exact daily credit allowance, how many points each action costs, or ticket prices (prices show on the purchase screen) — those are marked unverified. Pickle can make mistakes: check the task card and the result before paying or booking, and never type passwords or card numbers into the chat.
pickle-ai-free-agent-jpkr.source: Pickle official help centre (Japanese, checked 2026-11-19): Check your plan / How does the usage limit work? / Use reset tickets / Give your Pickle a task / Take over the browser; Pickle website and App Store listing

meta-muse-referral-1b-tokens.title: [US/CA/JP/SG/MX/AU] Meta Muse: enter an invite code within 48 hours, both get 1 billion tokens
meta-muse-referral-1b-tokens.highlight: Meta's personal AI agent Muse comes with its own Linux computer in the cloud (Muse Secure VM) and a full browser, so it can compare prices, book, email and order by itself; new users who enter a friend's invite code in Settings within 48 hours of joining get 1,000,000,000 tokens each, on top of the free weekly allowance.
meta-muse-referral-1b-tokens.regions: [US/CA/JP/SG/MX/AU] Only in markets where Meta has launched Muse: US (Sep 8), Canada (Sep 18), Japan (Oct 23), Singapore (Oct 27), Mexico (Nov 5), Australia (Nov 17). Elsewhere only a waitlist; an invite code does not bypass regional availability.
meta-muse-referral-1b-tokens.content:
Muse is Meta's personal AI agent, launched 2026-09-08, on iOS, Android, the web at muse.ai, Mac and WhatsApp. Every user gets a persistent Linux computer in the cloud (Muse Secure VM) with a full browser where the agent browses, fills forms and gets things done; sensitive actions such as sending email or paying need your approval first, and there is a complete audit trail. It connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, Instagram and more, and supports voice calls and custom Spaces.

Pricing: free with a weekly usage limit; Power is $20/month (500M tokens a week, 10 calls a day) and Maximum $100/month (3B tokens a week, 20 calls a day); when the allowance runs out you can wait for the refresh or buy additional tokens (purchased and promotional tokens don't expire).

Referral: on 2026-09-16 Meta's official @Muse account announced that you can invite up to 20 friends and that, once a friend onboards and redeems your code, each side gets 1 billion Muse tokens — up to 20 billion for the inviter. New users must redeem within 48 hours of creating the account; after that the option disappears and no code can be added.
meta-muse-referral-1b-tokens.conditions: 18 or older; must be located in a country where Muse is available (US, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Mexico, Australia); must be a new account and redeem within 48 hours of joining; one code per account; each code has a limited number of redemptions (Meta's copy says invite up to 20 friends; the exact per-code cap isn't published consistently).
steps: Sign up at muse.ai/join or in the Muse app with a Meta account (must be in a launched market; the web works)
Within 48 hours of joining open Settings: web Settings → General → Usage → Redeem invite code; app Settings → Redeem token
Enter your friend's invite code and confirm — each side gets 1 billion tokens, added on top of the weekly free allowance
Later, share your own code from Invite friends: each friend who redeems gives you another 1 billion (up to 20; filling all 20 unlocks early access to new features)
meta-muse-referral-1b-tokens.risk: Meta's help centre does not publish whether bonus tokens expire, how they are drawn down against a subscription allowance, or an official dollar value for 1 billion tokens (the ~$9 in this listing is our arithmetic at the Power rate, so it is unverified). Each code has a limited number of redemptions and public codes are often used up. Redeem only inside Settings in the app or on muse.ai; anyone asking for your password, a code, card details or money to "activate" a code is scamming you. Missing the 48-hour window cannot be fixed. Meta has not published the free tier's exact weekly token figure (Zuckerberg said about 100 million a week; it is not in the help page).
meta-muse-referral-1b-tokens.source: Meta's official @Muse post (2026-09-16) on the referral and 48-hour window; Meta Help Center "About Muse subscriptions" and "How to buy additional Muse tokens"; Meta Newsroom launch announcements by market (US from 2026-09-08, Australia 2026-11-17); checked 2026-11-19

aws-kiro-free-500-trial-credits.highlight: Kiro Free is a perpetual free tier: no card, 50 credits a month, with Claude Sonnet 4.5 and open-weight models such as DeepSeek 3.2 / MiniMax M2.5 / GLM-5 / Qwen3 Coder Next. From 2026-11-01, a first upgrade to Pro is free for the rest of the month (prorated to the second) and adds 500 trial credits (about $20, valid 12 months), unlocking Claude Opus 5.5 / GPT-5.6 Sol / Grok 4.7.
aws-kiro-free-500-trial-credits.regions: [Global] The free tier works with GitHub, Google or AWS Builder ID sign-in and needs no AWS account; paid plans need a billing address in a supported country (China, Japan, Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, the US, Canada and many more — full list on the pricing page), and some premium models are restricted by country; Enterprise and GovCloud have no free tier.
aws-kiro-free-500-trial-credits.content:
Kiro is AWS's AI IDE (IDE, CLI, Web, Crew) billed in credits: a simple prompt can cost less than one credit, a full spec task costs more, and models have different multipliers.

Free tier (perpetual): 50 credits a month, reset at the start of each month and not rolled over; access to Claude Sonnet 4.5 and open-weight models (DeepSeek 3.2, MiniMax M2.5, GLM-5, MiniMax M2.1, Qwen3 Coder Next) subject to rate limits; Kiro Web needs a paid plan, while the IDE and CLI work on Free.

The new free trial, from 2026-11-01 (announced 2026-10-27): the first time you upgrade from Free to Pro, the prorated cost of the rest of the month is covered, the first bill lands on the 1st of the following month, and you get 500 trial credits valid for 12 months that are used only after plan credits run out. Example: upgrading at 00:00 UTC on day 15 of a 30-day month gives a prorated $10.67 covered by the free month, so you pay $0 and receive 533 plan credits plus 500 trial credits. Starting on Pro+, Pro Max or Power still uses the free Pro month — you pay only the difference from Pro's prorated price ($10.67 for Pro+ in the same example). Going back to Free keeps unused trial credits, but they can then only be spent on free-tier models. The trial applies only to your first upgrade.
aws-kiro-free-500-trial-credits.conditions: The free tier needs no credit card (sign in with GitHub, Google or AWS Builder ID); upgrading to a paid plan requires a valid card and renews monthly. The 50 monthly credits reset and do not roll over. The 500 trial credits come once, on the first upgrade, expire after 12 months, and after a downgrade can only be used on free-tier models. Model availability depends on your country and each model provider's policy.
steps: Download Kiro IDE or the CLI at kiro.dev and sign in with GitHub, Google or AWS Builder ID to land on the Free tier (no card)
Use the 50 monthly credits to try Claude Sonnet 4.5 and DeepSeek 3.2 / MiniMax M2.5 / GLM-5 / Qwen3 Coder Next
For Claude Opus 5.5 / GPT-5.6 Sol / Grok 4.7, upgrade to Pro for the first time (card required): the rest of the month is free and you get 500 trial credits
Trial credits kick in after plan credits are used and stay valid for 12 months
To avoid the charge, downgrade to Free before billing on the 1st; unused trial credits remain usable on free-tier models
aws-kiro-free-500-trial-credits.risk: Upgrading needs a card, so forgetting to downgrade before the 1st means $20/month and up. The free month and 500 trial credits are first-upgrade-only; after a downgrade the trial credits are limited to free-tier models. The free tier's 50 credits a month don't accumulate and run out quickly on full spec tasks. Premium models are not available in every country. Kiro has not quantified the credit multiplier for each model, the Sonnet 4.5 rate limit, or the exact draw-down order of trial credits — those are marked unverified.
aws-kiro-free-500-trial-credits.source: Kiro official pricing page kiro.dev/pricing (including the free-trial FAQ), official blog "Kiro's new free trial gives you 500 extra credits" (2026-10-27) and kiro.dev/faq; checked 2026-11-19
