bot-hosting-net-free-panel.conditions: Free tier: 256MB RAM, 25% CPU, 512MB storage and one deployment, no credit card; renew manually in the panel every four days or the service stops; one free server per user; ads in the free panel; Node, Python, Go and Rust runtimes with custom ports supported; self-bots and other terms-violating uses are prohibited.
steps: Open bot-hosting.net and register, since the free tier needs no credit card
Create a deployment in the panel, pick a runtime such as Node.js or Python, and upload code from GitHub, a ZIP or the CLI
Set the start command and environment variables, and note the assigned port, static IP and free HTTPS subdomain
Return to the panel every four days to renew so the service keeps running
bot-hosting-net-free-panel.risk: Renewal every four days is manual and forgetting it stops the service; only one free server and the free panel carries ads; 256MB runs out on anything heavier and the process is killed; the official docs already cut free capacity for cost, so it can shrink again; abuse or terms violations lead to a ban.
bot-hosting-net-free-panel.source: bot-hosting.net official pricing page and docs (checked 21 November 2026: free tier resources, four-day manual renewal, any runtime and custom ports, new-panel free capacity notes) + official llms.txt + Space-Node free bot hosting comparison (3 November 2026)

katabump-free-pterodactyl-panel.title: [Global] KataBump free Pterodactyl panel host: 308MB and 716MB, Node.js and Python long-running processes
katabump-free-pterodactyl-panel.highlight: A Pterodactyl panel host whose free tier gives 308MB RAM, 716MB NVMe and 25% CPU with no credit card; Node.js and Python processes run long, with SFTP, web ZIP uploads, git clone and an editable start command
katabump-free-pterodactyl-panel.regions: [Global] Registered through a web panel with nodes in France and elsewhere; the free tier needs no card and is renewed by hand every four days
katabump-free-pterodactyl-panel.content:
KataBump hosts Pterodactyl panels for free: the free tier is 308MB RAM, 716MB NVMe storage, 25% CPU and I/O 100, with no credit card, and the official FAQ states plainly that the basic hosting plan is entirely free.

What it runs: Node.js with a required package.json and an index.js entry point, or Python with requirements.txt and main.py, installing dependencies with npm install or pip install on first start. Files go in by web ZIP upload (100MB per file), SFTP (at an address like sftp://fr-node-xx.katabump.fr:2022, with the server ID as the username) or git clone from the console, and environment variables, live logs and auto-start are included. The Startup tab lets you change the Node or Python version, the entry file and extra packages, and switch between the two runtimes at any time.

Renewal needs care: free servers must be renewed by hand every four days, and only within the two days before expiry; a lapsed server is suspended at once and its files are permanently deleted one day later with no recovery. Paid plans renew automatically. SQLite is free while MariaDB needs a paid plan, though external databases such as MongoDB Atlas can be attached.

What fits: Discord bots, scheduled jobs, webhook receivers, small APIs and static demos. The 308MB ceiling is hard, so builds and heavy applications do not run here.
katabump-free-pterodactyl-panel.conditions: Free tier: 308MB RAM, 716MB NVMe and 25% CPU with no credit card; renew by hand every four days, within the two days before expiry, or the server is suspended and its files are deleted one day later; SQLite only, with MariaDB on paid plans; self-bots and other terms-violating uses are prohibited; Node.js and Python with an editable start command.
steps: Register at dashboard.katabump.com without a card and create a free server
Choose the Node.js or Python runtime and upload package.json plus index.js, or requirements.txt plus main.py, over SFTP or with git clone
On the Startup tab at control.katabump.com confirm the entry file and start command
Start the server and watch the live log; click Renew now in the panel every four days to keep it alive
katabump-free-pterodactyl-panel.risk: The renewal window is only the two days before expiry, and missing it suspends the server and deletes the files a day later with no recovery; 308MB runs out on heavier applications and triggers automatic restarts; free plans have no backups and no MariaDB; most nodes are in France, so latency is mediocre at peak times; abuse or terms violations lead to a ban.
katabump-free-pterodactyl-panel.source: KataBump official docs FAQ, Plans and Renew Your Server (checked 21 November 2026: free tier 308MB / 716MB / 25%, four-day renewal, deletion one day after suspension, Node and Python support)

digitalplat-freedomain-dpdns.title: [Global] DigitalPlat FreeDomain: free .dpdns.org and .qzz.io names, ready for Cloudflare
digitalplat-freedomain-dpdns.highlight: The non-profit DigitalPlat gives away second-level domains: .dpdns.org, .qzz.io and .qd.je cost nothing to register or renew, and you delegate the NS records to Cloudflare to run DNS yourself; registration needs real WHOIS details and GitHub verification, with one domain per account by default
digitalplat-freedomain-dpdns.regions: [Global] Registered at dash.domain.digitalplat.org with no host lock-in and DNS delegated to Cloudflare or your own authoritative server; real name, address, phone and email are required
digitalplat-freedomain-dpdns.content:
DigitalPlat FreeDomain is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) free public domain service for individuals and projects, with a GitHub repository in the hundreds of thousands of stars and an official README claiming more than 500,000 domains registered. It is free to register and free to renew rather than free for a first year, and the listed suffixes are .dpdns.org, .us.kg, .qzz.io, .xx.kg and .qd.je.

What matters: it only handles name registration and NS delegation (bring your own DNS), while A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT and MX records live in Cloudflare or your own authoritative DNS. The typical flow is to add the full domain in Cloudflare first and note its two name servers, then enter the prefix, pick a suffix, paste the name servers and confirm the policies in the DigitalPlat dashboard, and finally add DNS records in Cloudflare once it is live.

The gates: registration asks for a real name, email, phone and contact address, with WHOIS possibly public unless you enable privacy protection, and needs GitHub-based verification. Each account gets one domain by default, and the official FAQ says starring the repository is not required. Whether a given suffix is free must be confirmed in the dashboard, since third-party guides disagree about .us.kg and .xx.kg. Renewal happens within 180 days before expiry and is free.

What it suits: personal homepages, portfolios, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages and Vercel demos, API demos, temporary test environments, and learning DNS and SSL.

What it does not suit: a commercial site or a single brand entry point. The project runs on donations, so suffix policies, quotas and upstream relationships can change; free suffixes carry weak reputation, so mail and ad network reviews get stricter; and control ultimately stays with the operator.
digitalplat-freedomain-dpdns.conditions: Register a DigitalPlat account with real WHOIS details and complete GitHub-based verification; one free domain per account by default, with quota and suffix availability set by the dashboard; external authoritative name servers such as Cloudflare's two are required; registration and renewal are free, with the renewal window in the 180 days before expiry; phishing and spam are prohibited and abusive domains are reclaimed.
steps: Add the full domain you want, such as myname.dpdns.org, in Cloudflare and note the two name servers it assigns
Register at dash.domain.digitalplat.org with your real name, email, phone and address, and complete GitHub verification
Under Domain Registration enter the prefix, choose a suffix such as .dpdns.org, paste Cloudflare's name servers and submit
After the NS delegation goes live add A or CNAME records in Cloudflare, and renew free in the dashboard within 180 days of expiry
digitalplat-freedomain-dpdns.risk: Free does not mean permanent: suffixes, quotas and renewal rules can change and the operator can adjust them; free suffixes carry low reputation, so mail and ad network reviews are harder; WHOIS needs real details and may be public; DNS control sits with a third party such as Cloudflare, so outages are yours to debug; not suitable as a commercial primary domain or sole entry point.
digitalplat-freedomain-dpdns.source: DigitalPlat FreeDomain official dashboard and FAQ (checked 21 November 2026: free suffix list, one domain per account, starring not required, bring your own DNS) + DigitalPlatDev/FreeDomain docs on GitHub + community guides from Dorabc, China-ChatGPT and SEUS (2026)

waifly-free-nodejs-panel.title: [Global] Waifly permanent free Node.js panel host: 300MB RAM, 1GB storage and one MySQL database
waifly-free-nodejs-panel.highlight: A Pterodactyl panel host in Paris with a permanent free tier at zero cost, no card and no time limit: 300MB RAM, 30% of a vCPU, 1GB storage, one MySQL database and one port, plus a live console, web file manager, SFTP, scheduled tasks and backups; a server offline for three days is suspended
waifly-free-nodejs-panel.regions: [Global] Registered on the web panel at dash.waifly.com with nodes in Paris FR1 and FR2; the free tier needs no credit card and allows one account per person
waifly-free-nodejs-panel.content:
Waifly is a French team's free Node.js host, and the official page is explicit: the free tier is permanently zero cost rather than a trial, with no expiry date, no credit card and no monthly hour quota, so the process keeps running.

The allocation: 300MB RAM, 30% of a single core, 1GB storage, one MySQL database and one port, running as a container under Pterodactyl on Proxmox and Docker. There is no root and no SSH, but you get a live console, a web file manager with an editor, SFTP, scheduled tasks, backups and DDoS protection on every plan.

How to start: sign up at dash.waifly.com, open Servers and create one, choosing the NodeJS Egg and the Paris FR1 or FR2 location; upload your project with package.json and dependencies install on start. On the Startup tab point the entry at your main file (node index.js or npm start) and read the port from the environment variable rather than hard-coding it. To use your own domain, point its A record at the server IP and declare the domain in domain management, where an Nginx reverse proxy is generated.

What fits: Discord bots, Express or Fastify REST APIs, Telegram bots, scheduled scrapers, webhook receivers and static sites behind Nginx all live inside 300MB, since Node itself takes about 40 to 50MB. What does not fit: building Next.js on the server, Puppeteer or headless Chrome, and audio or video transcoding, which start at the 4 euro Nano plan.

Risk rules: the anti-abuse policy suspends a server that stays offline for more than three days, and one account per person is enforced with an automated check every 30 minutes, so duplicate accounts get handled.
waifly-free-nodejs-panel.conditions: Free tier: 300MB RAM, 30% of a vCPU, 1GB storage, one MySQL database and one port, permanently zero cost with no card and no time limit; a server offline for more than three days is suspended automatically; one account per person with no duplicates; no root or SSH, with management through the panel, SFTP and MySQL only.
steps: Register at dash.waifly.com, since the free tier needs no credit card
Open Servers, click Create, choose the NodeJS Egg and the FR1 or FR2 location, and the free limits apply automatically
Upload the project with its package.json and set the entry file and start command on the Startup tab
Start it and read the npm install output and logs in the live console; keep the server online, since three days offline suspends it
waifly-free-nodejs-panel.risk: No root and no SSH means no system packages; 300MB is a hard ceiling, so builds and Puppeteer do not run; three days offline suspends the server, so the process must stay active; one account per person is enforced by automated checks; only Paris nodes are available, so latency from Asia is high.
waifly-free-nodejs-panel.source: Waifly official free Node.js hosting guide (updated 12 August 2026, written by the founder: 300MB, 1GB, MySQL, permanently free, three-day offline suspension, one account per person) + Waifly official site and docs.waifly.com

wispbyte-free-24-7-panel.title: [Global] Wispbyte free 24/7 panel host: 512MB RAM and 1GB of disk with no card, kept alive by logging in
wispbyte-free-24-7-panel.highlight: The official site says free hosting forever with no renewals and no credits needed: 512MB RAM, 1GB of disk and one always-on server with no credit card; logging into the panel once every 14 days keeps it, and since 31 October 2026 everything runs in Wispbyte's own client panel
wispbyte-free-24-7-panel.regions: [Global] Registered on the web panel at wispbyte.com/client, with Discord sign-in available; no credit card and one free server per account
wispbyte-free-24-7-panel.content:
Wispbyte is a free 24/7 hosting platform whose homepage states free hosting forever with no renewals and no credits needed. It suits Discord and Telegram bots, small Node or Python services and static sites.

The free tier: 512MB RAM, 1GB of disk, one server per account, always on with no sleep and automatic restarts, and no credit card or payment at sign-up. The keep-alive rule is one panel login every 14 days, and officially there is no renew button and no ad or coin grinding. Paid plans start at 4.99 euros a year for more memory and instances.

Important change, from the official 31 October 2026 announcement: the platform moved off Pterodactyl, where free.wispbyte.com and pro.wispbyte.com are now disabled for customers, and every server is managed in the Wispbyte client panel. Creating servers, uploading files and reading logs all happen in that one web console, without the old egg selector.

Sign-up and start-up: register at wispbyte.com/client, where Discord authorisation is fastest, then click Create Server in the dashboard, give it a name and description, upload code or connect a Git repository, set the start command and environment variables, and press Start. A reward ad may appear before Start, which is how the free tier is funded.

What fits: one always-on small bot, a light API, a webhook receiver or a scheduled job. The 512MB ceiling is hard, so large applications, multiple instances and heavy databases do not run here, and it is not a production environment.
wispbyte-free-24-7-panel.conditions: Free tier: 512MB RAM, 1GB disk, one server per account, always on with no sleep, no credit card and no renew button or credits; one panel login every 14 days keeps it alive; a reward ad may appear before Start; since 31 October 2026 management is only in the Wispbyte client panel, with the old Pterodactyl panel closed; abuse is prohibited.
steps: Register at wispbyte.com/client, where a Discord account is the fastest route and no payment is needed
In the dashboard click Create Server and fill in the server name and description
Upload code or connect a Git repository, then set the start command and environment variables
Press Start to run it, and log into the panel once every 14 days to keep it

vyce-cloud-free-vps.content:
Vyce.cloud is a small VPS host built around a free start, and the homepage is blunt: Vps-Mini is free, costs $0 and needs no card, with about two minutes from click to login.

Free tier specs: 1 CPU core, 2GB RAM and 6GB of disk, with root and SSH, a public IPv6 address and an in-browser terminal. Each server gets its own SSH port plus 19 ports for applications, 20 in total.

Renewal rules: the free server is not always on and must be renewed by hand in the dashboard. If you forget, the server powers off but your files stay, and it boots again after renewal; a free server left stopped for three days is deleted to make room. Free slots are limited and first come first served.

Access: sign-in uses a GitHub account at least 30 days old, which filters out bulk sign-ups, and no credit card is required. Paid plans are Vps-Plus at $1.99 a month for 2 cores, 4GB and 20GB, and Vps-Pro at $3.99 a month for 4 cores, 8GB and 40GB, bought with account credit for 30 days without renewal.

Our check on 21 November 2026: the location status on the homepage marks both Europe and Asia as Full right now, so free capacity is exhausted at this moment and you have to wait for a slot to free up or for the platform to expand; whether you can create one immediately is decided by the dashboard after sign-in.

steps: Open vyce.cloud and sign in with a GitHub account at least 30 days old, with no card needed
Under Choose your server pick the free Vps-Mini and create the server
After about two minutes, log in as root over SSH or in the browser terminal
Renew in the dashboard on schedule so the server is not stopped for three days and deleted

makefun-ai-agent-bounties-usdc.title: [Global] make.fun: AI agents win USDC on coding bounties, mostly free to enter, plus a top-1,000 participation reward
makefun-ai-agent-bounties-usdc.highlight: Build a bounty with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any other agent, submit a public repo plus the AI session transcripts, and a sandbox ranks entries on a published metric; rewards sit in an on-chain Solana escrow and pay out in USDC, most bounties are free to enter, and since 18 November a top-1,000 finish without a paid place still earns a small participation reward, claimable once the balance reaches $0.25
makefun-ai-agent-bounties-usdc.regions: [Global] An online platform open worldwide; needs a public GitHub repository, AI session transcripts and a Solana wallet for the USDC; some bounties require a linked GitHub, X or YouTube account or a specific Node version
makefun-ai-agent-bounties-usdc.content:
make.fun is a skill-based competition platform where AI agents build software for cash: each bounty states what to build, its reward and the metric it ranks on, and entrants use their own coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot or anything else) to build the work, then submit a public repository at one fixed commit plus the AI session transcripts that produced it. Automatic checks confirm the transcripts match the code, and a grader runs every entry the same way twice in a sandbox and ranks them on the published metric.

Money and settlement: each bounty's reward is locked in an on-chain escrow on Solana, with source at github.com/makefunai/prize-escrow so anyone can check the on-chain program against the code. Ranked winners claim from the escrow to their own wallet and the platform does not push payments; a few earlier bounties without an escrow are paid from make.fun's reward wallet and say so on the page. Officially, from 9 November 2026 make.fun has paid $5,967.50 in USDC to 413 accounts, each with a Solana transaction signature on record.

Free and costs: almost every bounty is free to enter, with no payment and no stake; a bounty with an entry fee says so and the fee goes into that bounty's pool. The real cost is your time and model calls, since the agent spends your own account's quota unless the bounty issues a sponsor-funded build key.

The 18 November change, from the official X account @makefunai: you no longer have to win to get paid. Finishing in the top 1,000 without taking a paid place splits an extra participation pool, more for a better finish; amounts are usually under a cent but stack across contests, the balance shows at the top of the site, and once it reaches $0.25 you press Claim and it goes to your Solana wallet in USDC.

What is live on 21 November 2026, with bounties opening and closing constantly: $35 poems and jokes, $50 spot-the-difference and poster art, $100 to $250 news images and data forecasts, $250 GTA 6 cover art and trophy guides, $500 video clipping or a 4KB Python chess engine, $1,000 for Bring the humans again, $1,325 for a token launch radar and $1,666 for Make GTA 6, alongside tasks that need a public X account or a YouTube channel.

The platform's own wording matters: a bounty is a competition, not a wage. Only the listed paid places earn anything, an entry outside them earns nothing, and make.fun promises no amount, so never value it at the headline reward.
makefun-ai-agent-bounties-usdc.conditions: Register a make.fun account and connect a Solana wallet for USDC; entries must be a public repository at one fixed commit plus the AI session transcripts that built it, and a failed automatic check does not count; most bounties are free to enter, with any entry fee shown on the page; model calls are on your own account unless the bounty provides a sponsor-funded build key; only the listed places carry a reward, with the top-1,000 participation reward as a small extra; claiming must happen inside the bounty's window of at least 7 days, after an automatic sanctions screen and a US tax form where the law requires one; unclaimed rewards return to the funding wallet.
steps: Sign up at make.fun and prepare a public GitHub repository and a Solana wallet
Pick a free-to-enter bounty under Live bounties and read its requirements, reward, paid places and deadline
Build the work with your own AI coding agent and submit the repository at one commit with the session transcripts
Wait for the automatic checks and two sandbox runs, then press Claim on your profile to move the USDC to your own Solana wallet
makefun-ai-agent-bounties-usdc.risk: Earnings are entirely unguaranteed: the platform calls a bounty a competition rather than a wage, an entry outside the paid places earns nothing, and participation rewards are often under a cent; model calls are your own cost and can exceed the reward; submitting requires public source and full session transcripts, exposing your code and prompts; claiming needs a sanctions screen and possibly a US tax form, and unclaimed rewards return to the funder; the platform only launched in November 2026, so its long-term policies and payout reliability are untested.
makefun-ai-agent-bounties-usdc.source: make.fun official homepage and documentation (checked 21 November 2026: most bounties free, rewards in on-chain escrow, $5,967.50 paid to 413 accounts, public repo plus transcripts required, rewards by rank) + official X account @makefunai announcement of 18 November 2026 (top-1,000 participation reward, claim from $0.25) + official escrow repository github.com/makefunai/prize-escrow

wells-fargo-everyday-checking-325.content: Wells Fargo's official offer page (accountoffers.wellsfargo.com/checkingoffer, read 21 November 2026) offers $325 to new checking customers who open Everyday Checking with at least $25, use the bonus offer code by 13 January 2027 and receive $1,000 or more in qualifying electronic deposits within 90 calendar days; the bonus is paid within 30 days of qualifying. Qualifying deposits include ACH payroll and government payments, RTP and FedNow instant payments, and third-party credits pushed to a debit card, while account-to-account transfers, mobile cheque deposits, Zelle and branch or ATM deposits do not count, and Early Pay Day deposits count only once they post. The $15 monthly fee is waived with $500 of monthly electronic deposits, a $1,500 daily balance, $5,000 in combined balances, or a primary owner aged 17 to 24. Several guides in mid-November described a $500 version ending 12 January; the official page rechecked on 19 November showed only $325 ending 13 January, so this entry follows the official page.
wells-fargo-everyday-checking-325.conditions: New checking customers who are the primary owner only; not available to anyone who received a Wells Fargo consumer checking bonus in the past 12 months, to employees, or to non-resident aliens and foreign entities signing Form W-8. Online applications can only open Everyday Checking, while branch applications may choose other eligible accounts but need a code by email first. The offer cannot be combined with other deposit offers, is one per customer, and the account must not be closed or restricted at payout.
steps: Open Everyday Checking from accountoffers.wellsfargo.com/checkingoffer so the code is applied automatically
Deposit at least $25 and route payroll or other qualifying electronic deposits into the account
Reach $1,000 within 90 days and check for the bonus within the following 30 days
Pick a fee waiver that fits you so the $15 monthly fee does not eat the bonus
wells-fargo-everyday-checking-325.risk: Third-party guides still quote $500 while the official page now shows $325, so trust the amount on your own application; the $15 monthly fee can eat most of the bonus; the bonus is taxable on a 1099-INT; closing early can trigger a clawback; non-residents signing Form W-8 are excluded outright.
wells-fargo-everyday-checking-325.source: Wells Fargo official offer page and terms (read 21 November 2026: $325, open by 13 January 2027, $1,000 in 90 days, Form W-8 signers excluded), Credit Guru (19 November 2026 recheck showing only $325 on the page) and usdailyrewards and Doctor of Credit (10 November 2026 reports of a $500 version)

amex-rewards-checking-300.title: [US] Amex Rewards Checking $300: $7,500 of direct deposits within 90 days (open by 1 February 2027)
amex-rewards-checking-300.highlight: Amex US consumer cardholders and Amex savings customers who open their first Rewards Checking by 1 February 2027 and take $7,500 of qualifying direct deposits within 90 days get $300 within 8 to 12 weeks, with no monthly fee or minimum balance
amex-rewards-checking-300.regions: [US] US holders of an Amex consumer card as primary or additional card member, or customers with an Amex High Yield Savings account or CD; a US tax ID and address are required
amex-rewards-checking-300.content: American Express's official welcome bonus terms, read 21 November 2026, pay $300 to customers who open their first American Express Rewards Checking account in their name by 1 February 2027 and receive at least $7,500 in qualifying direct deposits within the first 90 days, credited within 8 to 12 weeks of qualifying. The account has no monthly fee, no minimum balance, 1.00% APY, one Membership Rewards point per $2 of eligible debit card spending, fee-free withdrawals at Allpoint and MoneyPass ATMs, and support for Zelle and mobile cheque deposit. Eligibility is narrower than most bank bonuses: applications are open to US Basic Consumer Card members, additional card members on such accounts, and existing Amex High Yield Savings or CD customers, and Amex may ask for SSN or ITIN documents or notarisation. The account must be funded within 60 days to stay open.
amex-rewards-checking-300.conditions: Must already be an Amex US consumer card customer (primary or additional card member) or hold an Amex High Yield Savings account or CD; must never have had a Rewards Checking account, and only one is allowed per customer; $7,500 or more in qualifying direct deposits within 90 days, counting only ACH payroll, pension, government benefits or tax refunds, while person-to-person payments, account transfers, internal Amex savings transfers, cheques and points redemptions do not count; the account must stay open until the bonus is paid and funded within 60 days of opening.
steps: Confirm you hold an Amex US consumer card or Amex savings account or CD
Apply for Rewards Checking from the official American Express page
Fund the account within 60 days and route payroll direct deposits into it
Reach $7,500 within 90 days and check for the bonus within 8 to 12 weeks
amex-rewards-checking-300.risk: Open only to people who already have an Amex relationship, including a three-month card history, so many applicants are blocked; the $7,500 direct deposit bar is high; direct deposit rules are strict and P2P or transfers do not count; an unfunded account is closed after 60 days; the bonus is taxable interest.
amex-rewards-checking-300.source: American Express official welcome bonus terms PDF ($300, open by 1 February 2027, $7,500 in 90 days, paid in 8 to 12 weeks, read 21 November 2026), the official product page eligibility note, Frequent Miler (3 September 2026) and Perkful (19 November 2026 recheck)

icbc-global-travel-plus-2pct.title: [China] ICBC Global Travel Plus credit cards: 2% back on overseas spending, ¥500 a month on platinum (to 31 December)
icbc-global-travel-plus-2pct.highlight: ICBC Global Travel Plus cards on the Mastercard or Visa network earn 2% cashback on spending outside mainland China including Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, in stores or online, capped at ¥500 a month and ¥5,000 a year on platinum and ¥200 a month on gold
icbc-global-travel-plus-2pct.regions: [China] ICBC Global Travel Plus credit cards issued in mainland China on the Mastercard or Visa network; spending abroad and in Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, including online merchants
icbc-global-travel-plus-2pct.value: 2% cashback, ¥500 a month and ¥5,000 a year on platinum (≈$70 a month)
icbc-global-travel-plus-2pct.content: ICBC's official product page, read 21 November 2026, states 2% cashback on overseas spending from 1 January to 31 December 2026 for Global Travel Plus cards on the Mastercard or Visa network: purchases outside mainland China, including Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, in stores or online, may earn 2% back. Platinum cards are capped at the equivalent of ¥500 per customer per month and ¥5,000 a year, gold cards at ¥200 a month and ¥2,000 a year. Monthly pools of ¥209,000 for Visa and ¥349,000 for Mastercard apply on a first-come, first-served basis, and cashback is credited to the card in the transaction's billing currency the day after posting. Transactions routed through third-party payment providers do not qualify, nor do cash advances, transfers, repayments, refunds or reversals.
icbc-global-travel-plus-2pct.conditions: Limited to the ICBC Global Travel Plus card on the Mastercard or Visa network, with different caps for platinum and gold; the transaction must run over the Mastercard or Visa network, and third-party payment routing is excluded; overseas cash advances, transfers, repayments, refunds, tax refunds, reversals and cancellations do not count; the monthly pool is first come first served; caps are combined per customer across primary and supplementary cards.
steps: Confirm you hold an ICBC Global Travel Plus card and pay over the Mastercard or Visa network
Spend abroad or on cross-border shopping directly on the card network, not through Alipay or WeChat Pay
Check the cashback line the day after posting and watch whether the monthly pool has run out
Plan large purchases around the platinum or gold monthly cap
icbc-global-travel-plus-2pct.risk: Only the Global Travel Plus card qualifies, not other ICBC cards; the monthly pool is first come first served, so large purchases near month end can miss out; third-party payment routing never counts, so a habitual Alipay checkout earns nothing; overseas transactions still carry conversion costs that can exceed 2%.
icbc-global-travel-plus-2pct.source: ICBC's official Global Travel Plus credit card product page and benefit terms (1 January to 31 December 2026, ¥500 a month on platinum, ¥200 on gold, Visa and Mastercard monthly pools, read 21 November 2026), with FLYERT's overseas cashback coverage as the lead

boc-unionpay-overseas-3pct.title: [China] Bank of China UnionPay credit cards: 3% cashback on overseas offline spending, capped at ¥200 a month (to 31 December, enrolment required)
boc-unionpay-overseas-3pct.highlight: Mainland-issued Bank of China UnionPay credit cards earn 3% cashback on offline purchases through the UnionPay network abroad including Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, capped at ¥200 per person per month, after enrolling in the campaign
boc-unionpay-overseas-3pct.regions: [China] UnionPay credit cards issued by Bank of China in mainland China, including 62-prefix cards and 40/43-prefix Visa-UnionPay dual-brand cards; spending abroad and in Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan
boc-unionpay-overseas-3pct.content: Bank of China's card centre campaign, read 21 November 2026, runs from 8 April to 31 December 2026: cardholders earn 3% cashback on offline purchases settled through the UnionPay network outside mainland China, including Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, capped at ¥200 per cardholder per calendar month on the UnionPay channel. The reward pool for the campaign is ¥3.186 million, with ¥334,000 for April, June, July, September and November and ¥379,000 for May, August, October and December, allocated in UnionPay transaction order until it runs out. Cashback posts within 25 working days of the transaction posting to the card that made the month's first qualifying purchase. Enrolment is mandatory and earlier transactions are not counted; Bank of China neither enrols cards on your behalf nor allows retroactive enrolment.
boc-unionpay-overseas-3pct.conditions: Must be a UnionPay-badged credit card issued by Bank of China in mainland China (62-prefix single-brand or 40/43-prefix dual-brand), with supplementary cards enrolling separately; enrolment must be completed through the Bank of China credit card WeChat account or the Bank of China app with the cards ticked; only offline overseas transactions settled through UnionPay count, while Apple Pay in stores does, but cash advances, offline electronic cash, refunds, pre-authorisations and third-party payment routes such as Alipay and WeChat Pay do not; the monthly pool is first come first served; a replacement card must be enrolled again; refunded or reversed transactions earn nothing and paid cashback can be clawed back.
steps: Follow the Bank of China credit card WeChat account and bind your card, or open the Bank of China app
Go to Campaigns, cross-border enrolment, UnionPay overseas spending enrolment, tick the cards and confirm
Spend offline abroad or in Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan through the UnionPay network by card, tap, UnionPay QR or mobile tap
Check the statement line for the 3% cashback within 25 working days of the transaction posting
boc-unionpay-overseas-3pct.risk: Enrolment is mandatory and forgetting it means no cashback; the monthly pool runs out first come first served, so late-month large purchases may earn nothing; the terms say purchases may earn the reward rather than guaranteeing it; only UnionPay offline settlement counts, so online and third-party payment routes fail; overseas purchases carry currency conversion costs that eat into 3%; refunds claw back paid cashback.
boc-unionpay-overseas-3pct.source: Bank of China credit card official WeChat terms (8 April to 31 December 2026, 3% cashback, ¥200 monthly cap, ¥3.186 million pool and enrolment path, read 21 November 2026) plus the FLYERT card news article (a-524651) on the same campaign

octopus-mobile-welcome-150.title: [Hong Kong] HK$150 mobile Octopus new-customer welcome: add the card, spend HK$100 in one go, register (to 3 January 2027)
octopus-mobile-welcome-150.highlight: First-time mobile Octopus users who spend HK$100 or more in a single transaction and register on the promotion page get HK$150 of stored value, plus a free card face
octopus-mobile-welcome-150.regions: [Hong Kong] Mobile Octopus on iPhone and Apple Watch, Android Octopus, Smart Octopus in Samsung Pay, Huawei Wallet and Citi Octopus on iPhone; Android cards must also be added to Google Wallet, and cards added through the Octopus App for Tourists do not count
octopus-mobile-welcome-150.content: Octopus runs a mobile Octopus new-customer welcome from 5 November 2026 to 3 January 2027: customers who add a mobile Octopus for the first time (or move a physical card onto the phone) on a qualifying device, register the card number at octopus.com.hk/mo and then complete one transaction of HK$100 or more with that card receive HK$150 of Octopus stored value. The quota is 13,210 participants, first come first served. Android customers must also install the latest Octopus App, sign in to an Octopus Wallet account and add the Android Octopus to Google Wallet. The reward can be collected from the seventh day after qualifying, within 30 days, in the Octopus App or at an Octopus service point, and a free card face can be claimed until 10 January 2027.
octopus-mobile-welcome-150.conditions: The customer and device must never have had a mobile Octopus before the promotion period; cards added through the Octopus App for Tourists are excluded by clause 7. Top-ups, including card or wallet top-ups, are not spending, so a real merchant transaction of HK$100 or more is required. Registration must come before the qualifying spend, each participant gets one reward, and the card must still exist and not be refunded when the reward is claimed. Mobile Elder Octopus cards follow separate terms.
steps: Add a new mobile Octopus in the Octopus App or Apple Wallet, or move a physical card onto the phone
Register the full card number (including the digits in brackets) at octopus.com.hk/mo
Spend HK$100 or more in a single transaction with that card (top-ups do not count)
Turn on Octopus App notifications and collect the HK$150 within 30 days from day seven
octopus-mobile-welcome-150.risk: Tourist-app cards are excluded and many online guides wrongly use that route; Android phones need Google services and Google Wallet, which mainland models often lack; only 13,210 rewards exist; registering in the wrong order or mistyping the card number forfeits the reward; the value cannot be cashed out and removing or refunding the card cancels it.
octopus-mobile-welcome-150.source: Octopus official promotion page and terms PDF (5 November 2026 to 3 January 2027, 13,210 rewards, Android must use Google Wallet) plus an ecitizen.forum thread (20 November 2026) with a data point of no reward after spending on 15 November

usims-free-esim-1gb.title: [Global] USIMS free 1GB eSIM: works in 120+ countries, plus an always-on low-speed free tier (non-+86 number needed)
usims-free-esim-1gb.highlight: New accounts get a free first 1GB of global data in more than 120 countries; the homepage Activate Free Data tier adds an always-on 128kbps connection, and sign-up needs a real non-+86 number for the code
usims-free-esim-1gb.regions: [Global] More than 120 countries and regions including the US, UK, France, Germany, Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia and the Middle East; sign-up requires a real non-+86 number to receive the verification code
usims-free-esim-1gb.value: ≈$5 (first 1GB; the US 10GB/10-day pack is priced at $15)
usims-free-esim-1gb.content: USIMS states on its homepage that your first GB is on us: after downloading the app, registering and activating an eSIM, new users get 1GB of global data covering more than 120 countries. Reference prices are $15 for 10GB over 10 days in the US, $9 for ten days in France and the UK, and $10 for ten days in Germany and Spain. Beyond that 1GB, users report that Activate Free Data on the homepage issues an always-on low-speed profile of about 128kbps, enough for messaging, maps and WhatsApp, with traffic exiting through Orange in France; referrals pay both sides $3. The official page does not promise the low-speed tier will last, only the first-GB welcome gift.
usims-free-esim-1gb.conditions: An eSIM-capable phone and a real non-+86 number for the SMS code are required (a +372 Estonian number worked in one report, most virtual numbers fail); the first GB is for new accounts only; the low-speed profile is a separate data pack rather than part of the 1GB; if the eSIM does not appear right after activation, wait a minute and reopen the app.
steps: Download the USIMS app or sign up at usims.com
Verify with a real non-+86 phone number
Pick a destination, activate the eSIM and claim the free first GB
For the always-on low-speed tier, return to the homepage and tap Activate Free Data
usims-free-esim-1gb.risk: The low-speed tier runs at about 128kbps, so video and hotspot use are out; the official site does not commit to keeping that tier; +86 numbers cannot register and virtual numbers often fail; the first GB is a limited-time welcome gift and later data is paid; eSIM support and network locks still apply.
usims-free-esim-1gb.source: USIMS official site (read 21 November 2026: the first-GB gift and country pricing) and an ecitizen.forum thread (20 September 2026) covering the 128kbps tier and a +372 number test

google-ai-blackfriday-annual-50.title: [Multi-region] Google AI Plus / AI Pro annual Black Friday deal: up to 50% off, US Pro $99.99 for the first year (existing subscribers to Nov 26)
google-ai-blackfriday-annual-50.highlight: Accounts already paying for Google AI or Google One storage can switch to an annual AI Plus or AI Pro plan at up to 50% off until November 26 US time; accounts without a subscription get a separate offer from Black Friday, November 27
google-ai-blackfriday-annual-50.regions: [Multi-region] The discount depends on your account region and current plan (US Pro $99.99 a year, Taiwan NT$3,250); you must already pay for Google AI or Google One storage
google-ai-blackfriday-annual-50.content: Google opened its Black Friday early access on 20 November 2026: until 26 November (US time), accounts already paying for Google AI or Google One storage can switch to Google AI Plus or annual Google AI Pro at up to 50% off, with the exact discount set by the current plan and account. In the US, Google AI Pro (5 TB, Gemini 4 Neon, YouTube Premium Lite individual) drops from $199.99 to $99.99 for the first year and renews at $199.99 a year after twelve months; Taiwan's annual Pro falls from NT$6,500 to NT$3,250. Google AI Ultra (20 TB and 30 TB) and the 10 TB Pro tier are monthly only and excluded. Accounts without a subscription cannot see the offer yet; Google says a separate offer starts on Black Friday, 27 November.
google-ai-blackfriday-annual-50.conditions: Must already be a paying Google AI or Google One storage subscriber; free accounts are excluded. The discount is a ceiling of 50% and varies by plan, so the checkout page is the final price. Only AI Plus and annual AI Pro qualify; Ultra and 10 TB Pro do not. It cannot be combined with other Google One offers, and a student plan is usually cheaper. The first year renews at full price automatically, so cancel before the anniversary if you do not want that, and a valid Google Payments method is required.
steps: Open one.google.com/ai or the Google One all-plans page with the subscribed account
Check whether your account shows the annual discount (some see 50%, some only 25%, some nothing)
Pick annual Google AI Pro or AI Plus and confirm the first-year amount at checkout
Cancel before the year ends if you will not pay full price; the remaining period stays usable
google-ai-blackfriday-annual-50.risk: The discount varies by account and region, so the advertised 50% is not universal; the annual plan renews at full price and is easy to forget; student pricing or a family group may be cheaper; some regions or payment methods never see an annual option; changing region or payment method can cost you eligibility.
google-ai-blackfriday-annual-50.source: Google Gemini subscription lead Vikas Kansal's 20 November 2026 announcement, the official Google One plan page (checked 21 November 2026: US Pro $99.99 first year, $199.99 after), and an ecitizen.forum thread (21 November 2026)

a1-croatia-prepaid-esim.title: [Croatia] A1 Croatia prepaid eSIM: a +385 number cloud-activated for EUR 3 with EUR 3 back as credit, kept alive from EUR 2 for 92 days
a1-croatia-prepaid-esim.highlight: Buy the eSIM for EUR 3 on the official SIM-promo page; the QR code and number arrive by email and the EUR 3 comes back as account credit. A EUR 2-14 top-up buys 92 days, EUR 50-100 buys 360 days, and a 270-day window after expiry still receives SMS.
a1-croatia-prepaid-esim.regions: [Croatia] A +385 number opened entirely online (web form, QR code by email). The official flow asks only for name, email and phone, and no document upload is involved. China Mobile and China Unicom are the roaming partners in mainland China, and received SMS are not charged.
a1-croatia-prepaid-esim.value: EUR 3 starter (EUR 3 back as credit); about EUR 8 a year to keep
a1-croatia-prepaid-esim.content:
A1 Hrvatska is the Croatian arm of Austria's A1 Group. Its official SIM-promo page sells a prepaid eSIM for EUR 3: choose eSIM, enter an email address and contact details, pay online and the QR code arrives immediately by email; scan it, finish online activation and you hold a +385 number. The EUR 3 returns as account credit, as the official terms state that registering your details earns EUR 3. The same page offers a free physical SIM, but it ships only inside Croatia, so the eSIM is the only cloud-activated route.

Validity follows the official Uvjeti korištenja A1 usluge na bonove in force since 1 December 2025: a new card is valid 180 days, then each top-up adds days by amount - EUR 2-14 gives 92 days, EUR 15-29 gives 120, EUR 30-49 gives 180 and EUR 50-100 gives 360. Four minimum top-ups of EUR 2 cover about a year for roughly EUR 8, while a single EUR 50 top-up buys 360 days. After expiry a 270-day rescue window follows in which the number can only receive calls and SMS; one top-up inside it restores the line, and only after 270 days is the number closed.

Roaming and codes: A1's roaming partner list names China Mobile and China Unicom (4G/LTE) for mainland China, and the official roaming guide states that received SMS are not charged, so verification codes need no data package. With no balance left the line can still receive calls and texts, which suits it as a pure code-receiving card. VoWiFi is closed to prepaid: A1 support confirmed in writing that VoLTE is disabled on prepaid lines for marketing reasons, and VoWiFi exists only on business tariffs.

Caveats: ordering needs no passport upload (community tests through 2026), yet Croatian law does require prepaid users to be registered, so the details actually requested on the order page govern; payment needs a Visa or Mastercard that passes international checks; and the EUR 3 refund is a webshop promotion that may end at any time.
a1-croatia-prepaid-esim.conditions: Order the eSIM on the official SIM-promo page for EUR 3 with the QR code and number delivered by email and the EUR 3 returned as credit; outside Croatia only the eSIM is available (physical SIM ships inside Croatia only); validity per official terms: 180 days on activation, then 92 days for a EUR 2-14 top-up, 120 days for EUR 15-29, 180 days for EUR 30-49 and 360 days for EUR 50-100, with a 270-day window after expiry to top up and keep the number; the phone must support eSIM and be carrier unlocked; payment needs an international card.
steps: Choose the eSIM option on the official SIM-promo page, enter an email and contact details and pay EUR 3
Receive the QR code and number by email, install the eSIM and finish activation on the web page
Top up as needed: EUR 2 adds 92 days, or one EUR 50 top-up adds 360 days
Inside the 270-day window after expiry, one top-up keeps the number; after that it is closed
a1-croatia-prepaid-esim.risk: The EUR 3 credit-back is a webshop promotion that can end anytime; Croatian prepaid registration requirements apply and the order page's actual fields govern; validity depends on the top-up amount, so a small top-up buys only 92 days and the claim of EUR 2 keeping a number for a year does not hold; roaming in mainland China guarantees SMS reception only, as data is expensive; VoWiFi is closed to prepaid per A1 support; cards may fail fraud checks and credit is not refundable. Third-party eUICC: a community test in July 2026 found 9eSIM writes the profile but it is incompatible and never goes online, so use eSTK instead.
a1-croatia-prepaid-esim.source: A1 Hrvatska official SIM-promo page and the Uvjeti korištenja A1 usluge na bonove effective 1 December 2025 + official roaming tariff and partner network pages (checked 21 November 2026: China Mobile and China Unicom as partners in China, received SMS not charged) + Digital Residents forum thread on the Croatian A1 eSIM (2 April 2026)

vodafone-nl-prepaid-esim.title: [Netherlands] Vodafone Netherlands prepaid eSIM: a Dutch number from EUR 14 with no monthly fee, kept alive by one paid action every 6 months
vodafone-nl-prepaid-esim.highlight: Buy a prepaid eSIM on act.vodafone.nl: 7 days of unlimited data for EUR 14 (down from EUR 24), 14 days for EUR 24, 30 days for EUR 44, including a Dutch number that can receive SMS. Afterwards there is no monthly fee, and one paid use or top-up every 6 months keeps the number.
vodafone-nl-prepaid-esim.regions: [Netherlands] A +31 number bought online with an activation link or QR code and no document upload; 2GB a day roaming inside the EU; inbound SMS in China are free with sending at EUR 0.60; VoWiFi needs a Dutch IP and does not work abroad.
vodafone-nl-prepaid-esim.value: From EUR 14 (7 days unlimited data plus a Dutch number)
vodafone-nl-prepaid-esim.content:
Vodafone Netherlands' prepaid eSIM is one of the few routes to a real European number with no identity documents at all: order it on the official act.vodafone.nl/prepaid-esim page, pay, take the activation link or QR code, install it and you are online with a Dutch number that receives calls and SMS; making calls or sending texts requires a top-up first.

Prices on the official page: 7 days of unlimited data for EUR 14 (shown discounted from EUR 24), 14 days for EUR 24 and 30 days for EUR 44. Fair use allows 25GB a day in the Netherlands and 2GB a day roaming in the EU. Validity starts when the eSIM first connects to the network and uses data, and ends at 23:59 Dutch time on the 7th, 14th or 30th day; nothing renews automatically, so continuing means topping up and buying a new bundle.

Keeping the number concerns the prepaid account rather than the data bundle. Vodafone's prepaid FAQ states that credit and number stay as long as there is paid usage or a top-up, and that after six months without any paid action the account enters a restricted period (the first two months still receive calls and SMS) before the number closes. An SMS costs EUR 0.15, so the cheapest way to keep it is one small top-up or one text every six months.

Caveats: ordering needs no passport, proof of address or Dutch number, but payment usually needs an international card (community reports VISA works while some cards fail fraud checks). The Dutch retail prepaid range also offers a free SIM, a EUR 5 SIM with EUR 5 credit and a EUR 10 SIM with 2GB, all shipped to Dutch addresses. The official prepaid tariff charges nothing to receive SMS abroad including China and EUR 0.60 to send; Wi-Fi Calling is supported but needs a Dutch IP and is stated not to work from abroad.
vodafone-nl-prepaid-esim.conditions: Order and pay on act.vodafone.nl/prepaid-esim (an international card is needed); bundles are 7 days for EUR 14, 14 days for EUR 24 and 30 days for EUR 44, including a Dutch number that receives calls and SMS while outbound use needs a top-up; validity starts at the first data connection and does not auto-renew; keeping the number needs one paid action or top-up every 6 months; the phone must support eSIM and be unlocked.
steps: Choose the 7, 14 or 30 day bundle on act.vodafone.nl/prepaid-esim and pay
Install the eSIM from the activation link or QR code on the confirmation page or email
Top up the prepaid account before making calls or sending texts
Do one paid action every 6 months, such as a top-up or a EUR 0.15 text, to keep the number
vodafone-nl-prepaid-esim.risk: EUR 14 is a promotional price against a EUR 24 list price and moves with campaigns; this is a travel data product, so long-term keeping relies on separate top-ups and is bound by the 6-month rule; the eSIM includes no outbound call or SMS credit; inbound SMS in China are free with sending at EUR 0.60 and VoWiFi needs a Dutch IP; international cards can be declined. Third-party eUICC: a community test in September 2026 found 9eSIM cannot write this card because Vodafone profiles clash with ARA-M, so use eSTK or a native eSIM.
vodafone-nl-prepaid-esim.source: Vodafone Netherlands official prepaid eSIM page (checked 21 November 2026: 7 days EUR 14 down from EUR 24, 14 days EUR 24, 30 days EUR 44, Dutch number included, validity rules, 25GB daily fair use) + official prepaid FAQ on the 6-month keep-alive rule (relayed item by item in November 2026) + Digital Residents forum thread (13 October 2026)

asda-mobile-payg-esim.title: [UK] Asda Mobile pay-as-you-go eSIM: no monthly fee, 10p a text, kept alive by one paid action every 180 days plus free Wi-Fi calling
asda-mobile-payg-esim.highlight: A UK prepaid card on the Vodafone network: no monthly fee, 15p a minute, 10p a text and 10p a megabyte. One paid use or top-up every 180 days keeps the number, with a 90-day recovery window after that, and Wi-Fi calling is free for every customer.
asda-mobile-payg-esim.regions: [UK] A +44 number on the Vodafone network; choose the eSIM at checkout and download the QR code from the online account (phones only, no tablets or wearables); EU roaming across 46 countries comes with a plan, while mainland China sits in World Group with incoming calls at GBP 1.40 a minute.
asda-mobile-payg-esim.value: No monthly fee; kept alive for 10p every 180 days (about GBP 0.20 a year)
asda-mobile-payg-esim.content:
Asda Mobile is the MVNO of the British supermarket Asda, running on Vodafone. Its pay-as-you-go options, a one-month plan or plain per-use rates, need no credit check and no contract. Per-use rates are 15p a minute, 10p a text and 10p a megabyte with no monthly fee at all, which suits a number kept only for occasional use.

The keep-alive rule is spelled out officially: an account stays active for 180 days after activation, a top-up or a plan purchase, and every paid call, text, data session or top-up inside those 180 days resets the clock. After 180 days of silence the account is restricted (no outbound use, but incoming calls and texts still arrive), and another 90 days without action expires the number and the credit with it. One 10p text every six months is therefore enough to hold a UK number, which is why the forum rates it above Voxi for long-term keeping.

eSIM and Wi-Fi calling are the bonuses: pick the eSIM at checkout, download the QR code from the online account and switch between physical and eSIM for free; Wi-Fi calling is free for all customers and available seven days after activation for new ones, so in mainland China the UK number can take calls and texts over Wi-Fi instead of paying GBP 1.40 a minute to roam.

Caveats: top-ups only accept Visa and Mastercard registered to a UK address, the biggest hurdle for mainland users; eSIMs are phone-only; EU roaming across 46 countries comes with a plan, but mainland China is outside it, with incoming calls at GBP 1.40 a minute and texts at GBP 0.20, while the rate for received SMS is not listed officially and remains unverified.
asda-mobile-payg-esim.conditions: Choose the eSIM at checkout (phones only, not tablets or wearables) and download the QR code from the online account; per-use rates of 15p a minute, 10p a text and 10p a megabyte with no monthly fee; one paid use or top-up every 180 days keeps the number, with a 90-day recovery window after expiry; top-ups only accept Visa and Mastercard registered to a UK address; Wi-Fi calling is free and available seven days after activation for new customers.
steps: Choose a one-month plan or plain pay-as-you-go on the Asda Mobile site and select eSIM at checkout
Install and activate the eSIM from the QR code in the online account after paying
Top up or make one paid call or text within every 180 days to keep the number
In mainland China use Wi-Fi calling for calls and texts instead of roaming
asda-mobile-payg-esim.risk: Top-ups require a card registered to a UK address, so non-UK cards are often declined; 180 days without a paid action restricts the line and 270 days expires it with no credit refund; eSIMs are phone-only; roaming in mainland China costs GBP 1.40 a minute to receive calls and the received-SMS rate is not listed; Wi-Fi calling depends on network registration and is not promised to work from mainland China.
asda-mobile-payg-esim.source: Asda Mobile official eSIM, rates and charges, topping up and Wi-Fi calling pages (checked 21 November 2026: 15p calls, 10p texts, 10p per MB, 180 plus 90 day rules, UK-card top-up limit, free Wi-Fi calling) + Digital Residents forum thread comparing Asda with Voxi (12 November 2026)

lebara-uk-payg-esim.title: [UK] Lebara UK pay-as-you-go eSIM: no monthly fee, 19p a text, kept alive by one paid action every 90 days
lebara-uk-payg-esim.highlight: A UK prepaid card on the Vodafone network: no monthly fee, 25p a minute, 19p a text and 9p a megabyte. One paid call, text or data session every 90 days keeps it, with 365 days to restore a suspended line; the eSIM must be chosen at order and supply is limited.
lebara-uk-payg-esim.regions: [UK] A +44 number on the Vodafone network; the eSIM is chosen at order (community reports limited supply and some unsupported models); received SMS outside Roam Like Home destinations such as mainland China are free, with sending at 49p.
lebara-uk-payg-esim.value: No monthly fee; kept alive for 19p every 90 days (about GBP 0.80 a year)
lebara-uk-payg-esim.content:
Lebara is one of the most used UK number-keeping prepaid cards: it runs on Vodafone with no contract and no monthly fee, charging 25p a minute, 19p a text and 9p a megabyte, with top-ups from GBP 5 and no penalty for stopping.

Its keep-alive rule is stricter than most UK cards: one paid action (a call, a text or data) every 90 days, otherwise the balance is cleared and the SIM is temporarily suspended; a top-up or bundle purchase within the next 365 days restores it, after which it is permanently disconnected. Users also report 215-day reminder emails while customer service still quotes 90 days, and Lebara's community manager confirmed on 16 September 2026 that a line is suspended after 90 days of non-use and can be reactivated within a further 365 days. Budget one 19p text every 90 days, under GBP 1 a year.

eSIM is the weakest link: the website lets you choose an eSIM at order with a QR code by email that must be activated within 30 days, but community and comparison reports from October 2026 record limited eSIM supply for new customers and periods when only certain models qualify, one report naming only the iPhone Air. Confirm your model can select an eSIM on the order page, or start with a physical SIM and switch.

Caveats: ordering online needs no ID and no UK address, but non-UK billing addresses and foreign cards often trip UK fraud checks; received SMS outside Roam Like Home destinations, including mainland China, are free with sending at 49p; Wi-Fi Calling is confirmed on Lebara's own help page and FAQ for handsets on Vodafone's supported list.
lebara-uk-payg-esim.conditions: Pay-as-you-go with no monthly fee at 25p a minute, 19p a text and 9p a megabyte; one paid action every 90 days keeps the number, with 365 days to restore a suspended line before permanent disconnection; the eSIM is chosen at order and its QR code must be activated within 30 days, with limited supply and model support; non-UK cards are often declined.
steps: Choose a prepaid SIM or eSIM on the Lebara site and select eSIM at payment if offered
Install and activate the eSIM within 30 days of the QR code email arriving
Send one text or use a little data every 90 days to keep the number
Restore a suspended line by topping up or buying a bundle within 365 days
lebara-uk-payg-esim.risk: eSIM supply and model support are limited, so cloud activation is not guaranteed; the 90-day rule conflicts with 215-day reminder emails, so plan for 90 days; non-UK cards are frequently declined; received SMS in mainland China are free with sending at 49p; credit is not refundable.
lebara-uk-payg-esim.source: Lebara official pay-as-you-go page (restricted in November 2026, so rates and the 90-day rule follow the official community manager reply of 16 September 2026 and the ISPreview terms of 20 August 2025) + 4g.co.uk on eSIM for pay as you go (6 October 2026, limited eSIM models) + DeepChain eSIM data (31 October 2026) + Digital Residents forum thread on the Lebara EU plan (2 November 2026)

play-pl-prepaid-esim-rwk.title: [Poland] Play Poland prepaid eSIM: mandatory online identity check, and a PLN 100 top-up buys 365 days of validity
play-pl-prepaid-esim-rwk.highlight: Buy a prepaid eSIM online through Play24 or the website with free activation, but Polish law requires registration: a document plus a live photo check, or verification through a bank or mojeID. Validity scales with the top-up from 5 to 150 days, and the Rok Ważności Konta tier turns a PLN 100 top-up into 365 days.
play-pl-prepaid-esim-rwk.regions: [Poland] A +48 number whose online purchase requires registration with a passport or ID plus a live photo check, or a bank or mojeID check, alongside a PESEL or document number; EU roaming comes with the plan; inbound SMS roaming in China are free and VoWiFi works worldwide.
play-pl-prepaid-esim-rwk.value: PLN 100 for 365 days of validity (about USD 27)
play-pl-prepaid-esim-rwk.content:
Play is one of Poland's main carriers, and its prepaid eSIM can be bought entirely online: order on the website or in the Play24 app, finish registration online and the QR code arrives by email with free eSIM activation. Since March 2026 Play has offered photo verification (fotoweryfikacja), photographing a document and recording your face for remote checks instead of visiting a store; verification through electronic banking or mojeID also works.

Read the official price list for the money: basic rates are PLN 0.99 a minute or a text, top-ups run from PLN 5 to 300, and validity scales with the top-up amount: PLN 5-9 gives 5 days of outbound service, 10-29 gives 10 days, 30-49 gives 30 days, 50-99 gives 90 days and 100-300 gives 150 days, with longer incoming periods of 65 to 210 days. A single top-up covering a year needs the Play na Kartę Rok Ważności Konta tier, whose official price list gives PLN 100-300 a top-up of 365 days outbound and 455 days incoming; a PLN 20 Wydłużenie ważności konta extension also exists.

That is why the forum's figures of USD 7.82 to open and USD 1.30 to keep for a year have no matching tier in the official price list: the lowest PLN 5 top-up buys only 5 days, so a year means either one PLN 100 top-up or a top-up every 30 to 90 days. For long-term use the yearly cost runs from about PLN 20 for the extension service to PLN 100 for a full year of validity.

Caveats: registration is mandatory and an unregistered card cannot be used; the online photo check needs a document and a live face, and a passport works but may not pass first time; eSIM activation is free and switching a physical SIM to eSIM in store is free; EU roaming comes with the plan; Wi-Fi Calling is officially supported on prepaid and works worldwide for calls and SMS, so codes arrive anywhere with Wi-Fi, and inbound SMS roaming in China are free in the rate tables.
play-pl-prepaid-esim-rwk.conditions: The online purchase requires registration with a passport or ID plus a live photo check, or a bank or mojeID check, and a PESEL or document number; validity scales with the top-up from 5 to 150 days, and the Rok Ważności Konta tier gives 365 days outbound and 455 days incoming for a PLN 100 top-up; eSIM activation is free; the phone must support eSIM and be unlocked.
steps: Order a prepaid eSIM on the Play website or in the Play24 app
Complete registration as the page asks, with a document and live photo check or bank verification
Top up as needed: PLN 100 for 365 days, or smaller amounts for the 5 to 90 day tiers
For long gaps use the PLN 20 extension service or a tier-appropriate top-up
play-pl-prepaid-esim-rwk.risk: Mandatory registration is a real barrier and a passport plus live face check may be refused; the forum figure of USD 1.30 a year does not match the official price list, where the lowest PLN 5 top-up buys only 5 days; the PLN 100 year tier ties up more balance at once; inbound SMS roaming in China are free and Wi-Fi Calling is supported worldwide; the phone must support eSIM and be unlocked. Third-party eUICC: a community test in September 2026 found Play blocks the 9eSIM EID, so an eSTK-class (G+D chip) card is needed; test a download first to see whether the EID is blocked.
play-pl-prepaid-esim-rwk.source: Play official Cennik Taryfy Play na Kartę 3.0 from 1 June 2026 and the Rok Ważności Konta price list + official help page on registering and keeping a prepaid number (5 October 2026) + photo verification announcement (3 March 2026) + Digital Residents forum thread (27 September 2026)

ctexcel-hk-gba-prepaid.title: [Hong Kong] China Telecom HK Greater Bay Area stored-value card: a HK$100 face value and a +852 number, kept alive with HK$50 every 180 days (eSIM only in person in Hong Kong)
ctexcel-hk-gba-prepaid.highlight: No monthly fee and a real +852 number, with data shared across mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, and an official rule that HK$50 every 180 days extends the number another 180 days. Since November 2026 prepaid cards support eSIM, but only on Hong Kong and Macau model phones and only in person at the Wan Chai service counter.
ctexcel-hk-gba-prepaid.regions: [Hong Kong] A +852 number requiring registration (Hong Kong ID, or a qualifying travel document for non-holders, with BN(O) excluded); eSIM support since November 2026 is limited to Hong Kong and Macau model phones and needs an in-person application; data packages and SMS work while roaming in mainland China.
ctexcel-hk-gba-prepaid.value: A HK$100 card (kept alive for HK$50 every 180 days, about USD 13 a year)
ctexcel-hk-gba-prepaid.content:
China Telecom Hong Kong's (CTExcel) Greater Bay Area stored-value card, known locally as the blue card, carries no monthly fee and a real +852 number, with data packages shared across mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, which suits anyone who wants a Hong Kong number and data back in the mainland. The official stored-value page takes orders online with a common face value of HK$100, and Hong Kong local service requires registration first (Hong Kong ID, or a qualifying travel document for non-holders, with BN(O) excluded).

Keeping it is one of its selling points: per the stored-value terms and the card wallet, a top-up of at least HK$50 within every 180 days extends the number by another 180 days from the top-up date, roughly HK$100 a year, and the balance buys data packages that never renew automatically.

eSIM is the November 2026 change: China Telecom Hong Kong's official account announced that prepaid cards (the Greater Bay Area card and the HK$2-a-day Easy+ card) and postpaid plans now support eSIM, while annual cards and some roaming cards do not. Today only Hong Kong and Macau model phones qualify, and the application must be made in person at the service counter on 18/F, 108 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai (Monday to Friday 9:30-11:30 and 14:30-16:30). The first application is free with up to three downloads, replacement cards cost HK$30 and one replacement a year is free.

Caveats: this means it is not a cloud activation, since eSIM needs a visit to a Hong Kong counter; SMS and data packages work in the mainland, but data without a package is expensive; and the product is primarily a physical card whose loss costs a replacement fee.

A separate product often confused with it: travel eSIMs sold as China Telecom Hong Kong are usually third-party resale products and are not the same as this local stored-value card, so check before buying.
ctexcel-hk-gba-prepaid.conditions: Order on the official stored-value page (a HK$100 face value is common); Hong Kong local service requires registration; HK$50 every 180 days extends the number another 180 days; eSIM is limited to Hong Kong and Macau model phones and must be applied for in person at the Wan Chai counter in Hong Kong, free for the first application with up to three downloads and HK$30 for replacements; annual cards and some roaming cards do not support eSIM.
steps: Order the Greater Bay Area stored-value card on the official CTExcel Hong Kong page
Activate the card per the email instructions and complete registration
Top up HK$50 within every 180 days to keep the number, and buy data packages separately as needed
For eSIM, bring a Hong Kong or Macau model phone and your documents to the Wan Chai counter in Hong Kong
ctexcel-hk-gba-prepaid.risk: eSIM cannot be activated remotely and needs an in-person visit in Hong Kong; registration is mandatory; HK$50 every 180 days works out to about HK$100 a year; data roaming in the mainland is expensive without a package; a lost physical card costs HK$30 to replace; the exact data allowance follows the card wallet and current official page.
ctexcel-hk-gba-prepaid.source: China Telecom Hong Kong official stored-value card purchase and activation pages (checked 21 November 2026) + the carrier's eSIM announcement as reported by IT Home (3 November 2026: prepaid and postpaid support, Hong Kong and Macau model phones only, Wan Chai counter required) + stored-value terms of HK$50 every 180 days (third-party summary, 8 September 2026) + Digital Residents forum thread (30 October 2026)

starryblu-60sgd-signup.title: [Global] Starryblu sign-up bonus of up to S$60 in spending credit: register with an invite code and open a Singapore account and card with a passport
starryblu-60sgd-signup.highlight: The official X account still promoted up to S$60 in rewards on 19 November 2026; a mainland passport, a +86 phone number and an ID card as proof of address are enough to register, and the credit sits under My Vouchers in the app, applied automatically at checkout.
starryblu-60sgd-signup.regions: [Global] Open to a mainland passport, a +86 phone number and an ID card or bank statement as proof of address; the account and card are issued in Singapore by Wotransfer Pte Ltd, holding MAS major payment institution licence PS20200501.
starryblu-60sgd-signup.value: Up to S$60 in spending credit (about USD 45)
starryblu-60sgd-signup.content:
Starryblu is a multi-currency account from Singapore's Wotransfer, the sister company of Panda Remit holding MAS major payment institution licence PS20200501, and both its website and its official X account promote a newcomer reward: the post of 19 November 2026 still reads sign up and get up to S$60 in rewards.

The reward is spending credit, not cash. After registering and finishing KYC it appears under Me then My Vouchers in the app and is deducted automatically as a proportion of each card payment, which community tests put at roughly ten percent on small purchases, in effect a discount; the vouchers carry an expiry, recorded as one month, so a long wait in the queue can outlast them. An invite code must be entered at registration and cannot be added later, and registering without one usually yields only S$10.

The bar to open an account is low for mainland users: a Chinese passport, a face check, proof of address (a mainland ID card works) and a +86 phone number, all online, with approvals reported within minutes. The account holds CNY, SGD, USD, EUR, HKD, GBP and more; the virtual card is free and a physical card ships for about USD 9.9, though card applications still queue, with physical cards movable up a whitelist by the inviter while virtual cards simply wait.

Caveats: the credit is not cash and how much you actually get depends on later spending; this is a payment account rather than a bank deposit, so segregated custody is not deposit insurance; the invite and whitelist channels come from third-party inviters and the official rules change often, so the registration page in force governs.
starryblu-60sgd-signup.conditions: Register through an invite link or enter an invite code at sign-up, which cannot be added afterwards; a passport, face check and proof of address (a mainland ID card works); the S$60 arrives as several vouchers valid about one month and applied automatically at checkout; the virtual card is free but queues, and a physical card costs about USD 9.9.
steps: Register through an invite link or a registration page with the code prefilled, choosing China as country of residence with a +86 number
Complete passport, face and proof-of-address KYC in the app
Check Me then My Vouchers to confirm the S$60 credit arrived
Apply for the free virtual card and let the vouchers apply at checkout
starryblu-60sgd-signup.risk: The credit is not cash, applies proportionally and expires in about a month, so the real value falls well short of S$60; an invite code is mandatory; card queues can run months; the payment account is not a bank deposit; cross-border withdrawal and QR spending carry noticeable loss; the official rules change.
starryblu-60sgd-signup.source: Starryblu official X account post (19 November 2026: up to S$60 in rewards) + official blog and third-party tests (6 November 2026: vouchers under My Vouchers, valid one month, about 10 percent off, invite code cannot be added later) + Digital Residents forum thread on the S$60 bonus

urnetwork-free-tier-30gib.title: [Global] URnetwork free residential-exit VPN: 30 GiB a day, no card
urnetwork-free-tier-30gib.highlight: Get 30 GiB of free data every day (about 900 GiB a month) with no card and no trial, on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux, up to 2 devices at once.
urnetwork-free-tier-30gib.regions: [Global] Every platform on one account; exits are member residential connections in 108 countries and regions, so the countries you can pick depend on which providers are online at the time
urnetwork-free-tier-30gib.content: URnetwork is an open-source decentralized privacy network from BringYour, Inc. (Delaware, USA); its site counts 106,524 providers across 108 countries and regions. The free Community tier is neither a trial nor card-backed: every account gets 30 GiB of data at 00:00 UTC each day, about 900 GiB a month, and unused data does not carry over. When it runs out, new connections stop until the next refresh rather than slowing down. You can sign in with an email or phone number and password, Google, Apple or a wallet, or use an Instant Account that asks for nothing and shows a recovery phrase once. The free tier allows up to 2 devices online at a time, and Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux and the Chrome, Edge and Firefox extensions share one account; the system apps carry the whole device, the extension only the browser. The free tier also includes 5 HTTPS hosted proxies, while SOCKS5 and WireGuard profiles belong to UR Pro ($5/mo or $40/yr with 10 TiB a month). URnetwork publishes its Operator API and urn_ API keys for programmatic JWTs and exit selection.
urnetwork-free-tier-30gib.conditions: No card and no trial on the free tier; the allowance refreshes at 00:00 UTC and unused data does not carry over; up to 2 devices online at once; using other members' exits never requires sharing your own connection, and Provide defaults to Never; HTTPS hosted proxies only, with SOCKS5 and WireGuard in UR Pro; data counts in both directions and traffic between your own devices on one account counts too.
steps: Sign up at ur.io with an email or phone number and password, Google, Apple or a wallet; if you use an Instant Account, save the recovery phrase
Install the app on your phone or computer (Android, iOS, Windows, macOS or Linux) and sign in to the same account
Connect, keep Best available for automatic picking, or choose a low-latency country or city yourself
At 00:00 UTC the allowance resets to 30 GiB; when it runs out, wait for the refresh or buy a one-time data pack
urnetwork-free-tier-30gib.risk: Exits are members' home connections, so availability and latency swing with which providers are online, and no fixed node or uptime is promised on the free tier; residential addresses still hit bot checks and captchas; 30 GiB counts both directions and stops when used up; the free tier is capped at 2 devices and leaves SOCKS5 and WireGuard to UR Pro; before July 2026 the Android app shared your connection by default, new installs default to Never, so confirm Provide is set to Never under Account, Settings.
urnetwork-free-tier-30gib.source: URnetwork official plans page and docs at ur.io/products and ur.io/docs/about-your-data (rechecked 2026-11-21) + X community hands-on posts (@taiyanghere, 2026-11-21, and others)

klook-rewards-free-esim.title: [Global] Klook Rewards free eSIM: 500MB on sign-up, 2x1GB for Gold, 2x3GB for Platinum
klook-rewards-free-esim.highlight: Signing up for Klook already gives a 500MB / 1-day eSIM coupon with no booking; Gold members (USD 500 a year) get 2x1GB for 7 days and Platinum 2x3GB, taken off at checkout
klook-rewards-free-esim.regions: [Global] 100+ destinations; the coupon depends on your Klook Rewards tier (Explorer on sign-up, Gold at USD 500, Platinum at USD 1,500) and on what your market offers
klook-rewards-free-esim.content: Klook Rewards has a standing eSIM perk, still live on the official perks page on 2026-11-21: Explorer gets 1x500MB (1 day) just for registering; Gold, after USD 500 of completed bookings in 12 months, gets 2x1GB (7 days); Platinum, after a further USD 1,500, gets 2x3GB (7 days). Claim the coupon on the Rewards page, tap Use to open eligible eSIM products, and apply it at checkout. Klook notes the savings are capped, with the cap described in the promo code terms. Validity follows the tier period; unused coupons do not carry over.
klook-rewards-free-esim.conditions: Needs a free Klook account; the coupon matches your current tier; it must be applied to an eligible Klook eSIM product in the same order and cannot be cashed out or used as a standalone data plan; Gold and Platinum thresholds count completed bookings only; coupons expire with the tier.
steps: Register or sign in to Klook and open the Rewards page
Tap Claim on the eSIM perk to add the 500MB coupon to your account
Tap Use, pick a destination and an eligible eSIM plan
Apply the coupon at checkout, confirm the discount, and install the QR code from the email or app
klook-rewards-free-esim.risk: 500MB covers little more than landing tasks and maps; the discount is capped and some destinations or plans may not qualify; reaching Gold or Platinum means real spend, so chasing the tier is not worth it; coupons expire with the membership period.
klook-rewards-free-esim.source: Official Klook Rewards eSIM perk page (checked 2026-11-21: Explorer 1x500MB/1 day, Gold 2x1GB/7 days, Platinum 2x3GB/7 days) plus Klook's own rewards blog post

airfrance-klm-kolet-free-1gb.title: [FR/NL] Air France and KLM x Kolet: 1GB free for 2 days for Flying Blue members (codes AFKLDATA / FBDEAL)
airfrance-klm-kolet-free-1gb.highlight: KLM's official partner page states first-time Kolet users get 1GB free for 2 days across 190+ countries, with no flight booking needed, plus 10% off a first plan and 10 Flying Blue Miles per euro
airfrance-klm-kolet-free-1gb.regions: [FR/NL] Air France, KLM and Transavia France passengers and Flying Blue members; the eSIM itself covers 190+ destinations and claiming does not require a booking
